subproblem.title: Radon-measure compactness, convergence of restrictions, and a measurable slice-mass majorant (T1, T2, MM)
subproblem.statement: (T1) If U ⊆ ℝ^P is open and μ_j are Borel measures on ℝ^P with sup_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, then there are a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ and a Borel measure μ with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} → ∫ f dμ for every continuous f with compact support in U, limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U and μ(G) ≤ liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G) for open G ⊆ U. (T2) Let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, X_j ⇀ X in 𝒟_k(U), (μ_j, ξ_j) admissible representations of X_j and (μ_X, ξ_X) of X (Borel measures finite on compact subsets of U; a.e. strongly measurable k-vector fields with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; X_j(ω) = ∫ξ_j(ω)dμ_j and X(ω) = ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X on 𝒟^k(U)), μ a Borel measure finite on compact subsets of U with limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for every compact K ⊆ U, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous and t ∈ ℝ with μ{f = t} = 0. Then ∫_{f<t} ξ_j(ω) dμ_j → ∫_{f<t} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X for every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). (MM) Let μ_j be Borel measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ∈ ℝ≥0, with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for all j, and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all j and t ∈ (a, b). Then there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part I T1 and T2, and the paragraph "Measurable majorant (MM)". Notation: ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)| (Euclidean coefficient norm), ξ(ω) := x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)).

Part (T1): compactness of Radon measures.
1. If U = ∅ take φ := id and μ := 0; every assertion is trivial (the only compact/open subsets of U are empty and functions with tsupport in ∅ vanish). Assume U ≠ ∅ and put, for m ≥ 1, K_m := {x ∈ U : |x| ≤ m, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/m} (K_m := B̄_m(0) if U = ℝ^P). Each K_m is compact, K_m ⊆ int K_{m+1}, and ⋃_m K_m = U; every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_m.
2. For each m the measures μ_j restricted to K_m are finite measures on the compact metrizable space K_m with sup_j μ_j(K_m) < ∞ (hypothesis). SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable (applied on the subtype K_m to the pulled-back measures; its hypothesis ⨆_j μ_j(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ K_m holds by monotonicity) gives a subsequence along which ∫_{K_m} h dμ_j converges for every h ∈ C(K_m). A diagonal argument over m gives one strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every m and every h ∈ C(K_m), lim_j ∫_{K_m} h dμ_{φ(j)} exists.
3. For f continuous with compact support, tsupport f ⊆ U, choose m with tsupport f ⊆ K_m; then ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} = ∫_{K_m} f|_{K_m} dμ_{φ(j)} converges. Hence Λ(f) := lim_j ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} is defined on C_c(U) (functions on the locally compact Hausdorff, σ-compact space U, extended by 0); Λ is linear and positive.
4. Riesz–Markov–Kakutani (Mathlib RealRMK.rieszMeasure on the subtype U, which is locally compact as an open subset of ℝ^P, IsOpen.locallyCompactSpace) gives a Borel measure μ_U on U, finite on compact sets, with Λ(f) = ∫ f dμ_U. Let μ := the push-forward of μ_U by the inclusion U ↪ ℝ^P (a measurable embedding as U is open). Then μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, and ∫ f dμ = Λ(f) = lim_j ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} for every continuous f with compact support in U.
5. limsup on compact sets: let C ⊆ U be compact (if C = ∅ both sides vanish) and ε₀ > 0 with C_{ε₀} := {dist(·, C) ≤ ε₀} ⊆ U. For 0 < ε ≤ ε₀ choose (Urysohn) f continuous, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on C, f = 0 off {dist(·, C) < ε}; then μ_{φ(j)}(C) ≤ ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} → ∫ f dμ ≤ μ(C_ε). Thus limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(C) ≤ μ(C_ε) for every ε ∈ (0, ε₀]; as ε ↓ 0, C_ε ↓ C (C closed) and μ(C_{ε₀}) < ∞, so μ(C_ε) → μ(C) and limsup_j μ_{φ(j)}(C) ≤ μ(C).
6. liminf on open sets: let G ⊆ U be open. For compact C ⊆ G choose f continuous, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, f = 1 on C, tsupport f ⊆ G compact; then μ(C) ≤ ∫ f dμ = lim_j ∫ f dμ_{φ(j)} ≤ liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G). G is the increasing union of countably many compact sets C_m, so μ(G) = sup_m μ(C_m) ≤ liminf_j μ_{φ(j)}(G).

Part (T2): convergence of restrictions.
7. Fix ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U); C := tsupport ω is compact ⊆ U and ‖ω‖_∞ < ∞. Put a_j := ∫_{f<t} ξ_j(ω) dμ_j and a := ∫_{f<t} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X. These are absolutely convergent: μ_j-a.e. (resp. μ_X-a.e.) |ξ_j(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞1_C(x), and μ_j(C), μ_X(C) < ∞.
8. Let ε > 0. The compact sets C₁ := C ∩ {f ≤ t − ε} and C₂ := C ∩ {f ≥ t} are disjoint (f continuous). Choose χ_ε ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in the open set U ∖ C₂ and χ_ε = 1 on C₁ (smooth Urysohn function for the compact set C₁ inside the open set U ∖ C₂). Then χ_εω ∈ 𝒟^k(U).
9. On C we have 1_{f<t} − χ_ε = 0 where f ≤ t − ε (1 − 1) and where f ≥ t (0 − 0), and |1_{f<t} − χ_ε| ≤ 1 everywhere; ω = 0 off C. As ξ_j(x) is linear, X_j(χ_εω) = ∫ χ_ε ξ_j(ω) dμ_j, hence |a_j − X_j(χ_εω)| = |∫ (1_{f<t} − χ_ε) ξ_j(ω) dμ_j| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ μ_j(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}), and likewise |a − X(χ_εω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ μ_X(C ∩ {t − ε < f < t}).
10. C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t} is a compact subset of U, so limsup_j μ_j(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) ≤ μ(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) by hypothesis, and X_j(χ_εω) → X(χ_εω) by weak convergence. Therefore limsup_j |a_j − a| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ (μ(C ∩ {t − ε ≤ f ≤ t}) + μ_X(C ∩ {t − ε < f < t})).
11. Let ε = 1/m → 0. The sets C ∩ {t − 1/m ≤ f ≤ t} decrease to C ∩ {f = t} and μ(C) < ∞, so their μ-measures tend to μ(C ∩ {f = t}) ≤ μ{f = t} = 0; the sets C ∩ {t − 1/m < f < t} decrease to ∅ and μ_X(C) < ∞, so their μ_X-measures tend to 0. Hence limsup_j |a_j − a| = 0, i.e. a_j → a.

Part (MM): measurable majorant of slice masses.
12. If b ≤ a then Ioo a b = ∅ and g := 0 works. Let a < b. For each j define F_j : ℝ → ℝ, F_j(t) := (μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < min(t, b)})).toReal. The sets increase with t and are contained in G ∩ {a < f < b}, of finite μ_j-measure, so F_j is nondecreasing, F_j(a) = 0 and F_j(b) = (μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b})).toReal.
13. Let t ∈ (a, b) and 0 < h < t − a. The set S := {t − h < f < t} is Borel (f continuous), so for the (arbitrary) set E := G ∩ {a < f < t}, μ_j(E) = μ_j(E ∩ S) + μ_j(E ∖ S) (Mathlib measure_inter_add_sdiff), with E ∩ S = G ∩ {t − h < f < t} and E ∖ S ⊇ G ∩ {a < f < t − h}. All quantities are finite, so μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ≤ F_j(t) − F_j(t − h).
14. A monotone function ℝ → ℝ is differentiable a.e. (Mathlib Monotone.ae_differentiableAt); the union over j of the exceptional sets is null. If F_j is differentiable at t ∈ (a, b), then by step 13 ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ≤ ofReal((F_j(t) − F_j(t − h))/h) → ofReal(F_j'(t)) as h ↓ 0, so liminf_{h↓0} ofReal(h⁻¹)μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) ≤ ofReal(F_j'(t)) and, by the hypothesis, Z_j(t) ≤ L·ofReal(F_j'(t)).
15. Define g(t) := L · liminf_j ofReal(deriv F_j t). Each deriv F_j is measurable (Mathlib measurable_deriv), hence g is measurable. By step 14, for a.e. t ∈ (a, b): liminf_j Z_j(t) ≤ liminf_j (L·ofReal(F_j'(t))) = L·liminf_j ofReal(F_j'(t)) = g(t) (multiplication by the finite constant L is monotone and continuous on [0, ∞], so it commutes with liminf).
16. deriv F_j ≥ 0 (F_j is nondecreasing; where it is not differentiable deriv F_j = 0), deriv F_j is integrable on [a, b] (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegrable_deriv) and ∫_a^b deriv F_j ≤ F_j(b) − F_j(a) (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc). Hence ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F_j) = ofReal(∫_a^b deriv F_j) ≤ μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). By Fatou's lemma for measurable functions (Mathlib lintegral_liminf_le), ∫⁻_{(a,b)} g = L ∫⁻_{(a,b)} liminf_j ofReal(deriv F_j) ≤ L liminf_j ∫⁻_{(a,b)} ofReal(deriv F_j) ≤ L liminf_j μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). This proves (MM). ∎

Remark (how siblings use (MM)): if μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}) ≤ Λ < ∞ for all j, then ∫⁻ g < ∞, so g < ∞ a.e. and liminf_j Z_j(t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (a, b) (for a constant sequence: Z(t) < ∞ a.e.); if μ_j(G ∩ {a<f<b}) → 0, then g = 0 a.e. and liminf_j Z_j(t) = 0 for a.e. t ∈ (a, b).
proof_key_steps: T1: exhaust U by compacts K_m, apply SimonGMT simon_theorem_4_16_compact_metrizable on each K_m and diagonalize.
T1: the limit functional on C_c(U) is positive linear; Riesz–Markov–Kakutani gives μ, pushed forward to ℝ^P.
T1: Urysohn approximations from above (compact sets) and below (open sets) give the limsup/liminf inequalities.
T2: for ε > 0 a smooth cutoff χ_ε ≡ 1 on C ∩ {f ≤ t−ε}, ≡ 0 on C ∩ {f ≥ t} reduces the restricted integrals to X_j(χ_εω) up to ‖ω‖_∞μ_j(C ∩ {t−ε ≤ f ≤ t}).
T2: limsup on the compact level band and μ{f = t} = 0, μ_X-continuity from above, and X_j(χ_εω) → X(χ_εω) give convergence.
MM: F_j(t) := μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < min(t,b)}) is monotone; the slice bound gives Z_j ≤ L F_j' wherever F_j is differentiable (a.e.).
MM: g := L liminf_j F_j' is measurable and Fatou with ∫_a^b F_j' ≤ F_j(b) − F_j(a) gives the integral bound.

audit.reason: All three conjuncts match their prose. Exhaustion and diagonal compactness yield T1; the one-sided cutoff argument proves T2 without requiring the target representation to vanish on the level set. MM correctly handles arbitrary G by splitting along measurable strips, then applying differentiation and Fatou.

subproblem.title: Isoperimetric filling with support control (Simon 6.1 via the deformation theorem)
subproblem.statement: Assume (DT), the exact frozen statement of the parent node's dependency theorem cmc_deformation_theorem (assumed as a hypothesis since it is not available to this child). For all P, m ∈ ℕ there is a real c ≥ 1 such that every integer multiplicity Z ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with compact support, ∂Z = 0 and M(Z) < ∞ is the boundary of an integer multiplicity Y ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with M(Y) ≤ c(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}M(Z) and spt Y ⊆ {x : dist(x, spt Z) < 3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}} (Metric.thickening).
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (P m : ℕ), ∃ c : NNReal, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (ρ : ℝ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (Λ : NNReal), 0 < ρ → IsCompact K → ∃ 𝒬 : Set (GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), 𝒬.Finite ∧ ∀ T : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity T → T.support ⊆ K → T.mass ≤ Λ → T.boundary.mass < ∞ → ∃ Q ∈ 𝒬, ∃ (R : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2)) (S : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), IsIntegerMultiplicity Q ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity Q.boundary ∧ IsIntegerMultiplicity R ∧ T - Q - S = R.boundary ∧ (Q = 0 ∨ ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ (m + 1)) ≤ Q.mass) ∧ Q.mass ≤ c * T.mass ∧ Q.boundary.mass ≤ c * T.boundary.mass ∧ R.mass ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ * T.mass ∧ S.mass ≤ c * ENNReal.ofReal ρ * T.boundary.mass ∧ Q.support ∪ R.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * ρ) T.support ∧ Q.boundary.support ∪ S.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * ρ) T.boundary.support) → ∀ (P m : ℕ), ∃ c : ℝ, 1 ≤ c ∧ ∀ Z : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), IsIntegerMultiplicity Z → IsCompact Z.support → Z.boundary = 0 → Z.mass < ∞ → ∃ Y : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 2), IsIntegerMultiplicity Y ∧ Y.boundary = Z ∧ Y.mass ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (c * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1)) * Z.mass.toReal) ∧ Y.support ⊆ thickening (3 * Real.sqrt P * (2 * c * Z.mass.toReal) ^ ((1 : ℝ) / (m + 1))) Z.support
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, V3 "(Iso)" (Simon Ch. 6, 6.1 via the deformation theorem 6.2, with the support of the filling controlled by (DT)), re-indexed with m := d − 1 so that Z has degree m + 1. (DT) is the exact frozen statement of the parent node's dependency theorem cmc_deformation_theorem (not available to this child, hence assumed). M(X) := X.mass = M_{ℝ^P}(X); ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|.

1. Let c ≥ 1 (a real number; (DT) provides c ∈ ℝ≥0 with 1 ≤ c) be the constant of (DT) for (P, m). Let Z be IM in 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) with spt Z compact, ∂Z = 0 and z := M(Z) < ∞ (so z ∈ [0, ∞) and z = M(Z).toReal).
2. Mass zero means zero. If X ∈ 𝒟_k(ℝ^P) has M(X) = 0 then X = 0: for ω with ‖ω‖_∞ ≤ 1 both ω and −ω are admissible (the Euclidean coefficient norm is even), so X(ω) ≤ 0 and −X(ω) ≤ 0; for a general ω, ±sω is admissible for every s > 0 with s‖ω‖_∞ ≤ 1 (‖ω‖_∞ < ∞ since ω is continuous with compact support), so ±X(ω) ≤ 0.
3. The zero current is IM (IMRep with empty carrier, mult 0, orient 0; ∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable by SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero, the remaining fields are vacuous as Hᵏ⌞∅ = 0) and has empty support (every bounded open set lies in its zero region), and 0 has boundary 0.
4. Case z = 0. By step 2, Z = 0. Take Y := 0: Y is IM, ∂Y = 0 = Z, M(Y) = 0 = c·(2c·0)^{1/(m+1)}·0, and spt Y = ∅ ⊆ thickening(3√P·(2c·0)^{1/(m+1)}, spt Z).
5. Case z > 0. Put ρ := (2cz)^{1/(m+1)} > 0, so ρ^{m+1} = 2cz. Apply (DT) with this ρ, K := spt Z (compact) and Λ := z ∈ ℝ≥0 to T := Z: Z is IM, spt Z ⊆ K, M(Z) ≤ Λ and M(∂Z) = M(0) = 0 < ∞. This gives Q, S ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(ℝ^P) and R ∈ 𝒟_{m+2}(ℝ^P) with Q, ∂Q, R IM, Z − Q − S = ∂R, (Q = 0 or M(Q) ≥ ρ^{m+1}), M(Q) ≤ c·M(Z) = cz, M(R) ≤ c·ρ·M(Z), M(S) ≤ c·ρ·M(∂Z) = 0, and spt Q ∪ spt R ⊆ thickening(3√P ρ, spt Z).
6. M(S) = 0, so S = 0 (step 2). M(Q) ≤ cz < 2cz = ρ^{m+1} (as z > 0 and c ≥ 1 > 0), so the alternative M(Q) ≥ ρ^{m+1} is impossible and Q = 0. Therefore Z = Z − 0 − 0 = ∂R (equality of currents, checked on every test form).
7. Y := R is IM, ∂Y = Z, M(Y) ≤ cρz = c(2cz)^{1/(m+1)}z, i.e. M(Y) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal(c·(2c·M(Z).toReal)^{1/(m+1)}·M(Z).toReal), and spt Y ⊆ thickening(3√P(2c·M(Z).toReal)^{1/(m+1)}, spt Z). The same constant c works for all Z, which proves the statement. ∎

Remark (form used by siblings): with c_I := c(2c)^{1/(m+1)}, M(Y) ≤ c_I M(Z)^{(m+2)/(m+1)}.
proof_key_steps: Take c from (DT) for (P, m); a current of zero mass is zero.
If M(Z) = 0 then Z = 0 and Y := 0 works.
Otherwise apply (DT) with ρ := (2cM(Z))^{1/(m+1)}, K := spt Z, Λ := M(Z).
M(S) ≤ cρM(∂Z) = 0 gives S = 0; M(Q) ≤ cM(Z) < ρ^{m+1} and the dichotomy give Q = 0.
Hence Z = ∂R with the mass and support bounds of (DT); take Y := R.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes almost everywhere imply countable rectifiability (Simon Ch. 3, 1.6 ⇐, corrected constant)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, M ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), and Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces of ℝ^P such that x ↦ (orthogonal projection onto Q(x)) is Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable and M has approximate tangent space Q(x) at Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x)). Then M is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable n M).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet M → μHE[n] M ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (Q x).starProjection) (μHE[n].restrict M) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict M), HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x (Q x)) → CountablyRectifiable n M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, V13 (Simon Ch. 3, Theorem 1.6 "⇐", chapter-03.txt lines 107–300, with the corrected constant ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n} needed for the contradiction in (10)). The parent's iteration "A ∖ ⋃F_k(ℝⁿ)" is replaced by running the same construction with an arbitrary error ε' > 0 (step 10), so that no locality of approximate tangent spaces for subsets is needed. Hⁿ := μHE[n], μ := Hⁿ⌞M (a finite Borel measure), p_V := orthogonal projection onto a subspace V (starProjection), ‖·‖ the operator norm, ω_n := Lⁿ(B_1).

0. Trivial cases. If Hⁿ(M) = 0, M is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero). If n = 0: H⁰ is the counting measure, so H⁰(M) < ∞ means M is finite; each point is the range of a constant (Lipschitz) map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P (SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range, countablyRectifiable_iUnion). If n > P: μHE[n] = 0 on ℝ^P (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top with d₁ := P, d₂ := n, using that μHE[P] = Lebesgue measure is σ-finite: every bounded set has finite μHE[P]-measure, hence μHE[n]-measure 0), so Hⁿ(M) = 0. If n = P: M ⊆ ℝ^P = range of the identity of Euclid P (Lipschitz). Henceforth 1 ≤ n < P, ℓ := P − n ≥ 1, and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x) holds for μ-a.e. x (so dim Q(x) = n and π_x := Q(x)^⊥ has dimension ℓ).
1. Cones. For an ℓ-dimensional subspace π and α > 0 let X_α(π, x) := {y : dist(y − x, π) < α|y − x|} (open; x ∉ X_α(π, x)). Recall dist(v, π) = |v − p_π v|, so |dist(v, π) − dist(v, π')| ≤ ‖p_π − p_{π'}‖ |v|.
2. Densities at tangent points. Let x satisfy HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x). Write ν_ρ := Hⁿ⌞(blowUpMap x ρ '' M), blowUpMap x ρ (y) = ρ⁻¹(y − x). By translation invariance and scaling of Hⁿ, ν_ρ(S) = ρ^{−n}μ(x + ρS). The definition says ∫ f dν_ρ → ∫ f dHⁿ⌞Q(x) as ρ ↓ 0 for all f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P). Approximating indicators by continuous compactly supported functions from below (open bounded sets O) and from above (compact sets F'): liminf ν_ρ(O) ≥ Hⁿ(Q(x) ∩ O), limsup ν_ρ(F') ≤ Hⁿ(Q(x) ∩ F'). With O := B_1, F' := B̄_1 and Hⁿ(Q(x) ∩ ∂B_1) = 0: (5) μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) → Hⁿ(Q(x) ∩ B_1)/ω_n = 1. With F' := X̄ ∩ B̄_1, X̄ := {y : dist(y, π_x) ≤ |y|/2} (closed), we have F' ∩ Q(x) = {0} (for v ∈ Q(x), dist(v, π_x) = |v|) and Hⁿ({0}) = 0 (n ≥ 1), so (6) μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) ≤ ν_ρ(F')/ω_n → 0.
3. Fix ε' > 0. Lusin. The map x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, hence μ-a.e. equal to a Borel map q; let M₁ ⊆ M be a Borel set of full μ-measure on which q(x) = p_{Q(x)} and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x) hold. μ is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence closed-inner regular; applying SimonGMT Chapter01 exists_isClosed_continuousOn_of_measurable to the finitely many matrix entries of q on M₁ and intersecting the closed sets obtained, we get a closed F ⊆ M₁ with μ(M ∖ F) ≤ ε'/4 on which x ↦ p_{Q(x)} (hence x ↦ p_{π_x} = I − p_{Q(x)}) is continuous; (5) and (6) hold at every x ∈ F.
4. Egorov. For x ∈ F and k ≥ 1 put f_k(x) := inf_{ρ∈ℚ∩(0,1/k)} μ(B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) and q_k(x) := sup_{ρ∈ℚ∩(0,1/k)} μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ). For fixed ρ, x ↦ μ(B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous and, on F, x ↦ μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) is lower semicontinuous (the set {(x, y) ∈ F × ℝ^P : dist(y − x, π_x) < |y − x|/2, |y − x| < ρ} is relatively open by continuity of x ↦ p_{π_x}; Fatou); countable infima/suprema of semicontinuous functions are Borel. Both quotients are left continuous in ρ (open balls and open cones increase to their union), so f_k and q_k are also the inf/sup over all ρ ∈ (0, 1/k); by (5), (6), f_k → 1 and q_k → 0 pointwise on F. Extend f_k, q_k by 0 off the closed set F (so they are Borel on ℝ^P). By Egorov's theorem (Mathlib MeasureTheory.tendstoUniformlyOn_of_ae_tendsto for the finite measure μ⌞F) and closed inner regularity, there is a closed E₁ ⊆ F with μ(F ∖ E₁) ≤ ε'/4 on which the convergence is uniform. Choose R₀ with μ(ℝ^P ∖ B̄_{R₀}(0)) ≤ ε'/4 and put E := E₁ ∩ B̄_{R₀}(0): E is compact and μ(M ∖ E) ≤ 3ε'/4 < ε'.
5. Uniform density bounds. Let ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n}. By uniform convergence there is δ > 0 such that for all x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ: μ(B_ρ(x)) ≥ (1 − ε)ω_nρⁿ and μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ εω_nρⁿ.
6. Net of planes. The set of orthogonal projections of rank ℓ is compact in the space of linear maps, so there are ℓ-dimensional subspaces π_1, …, π_N such that every ℓ-dimensional π has ‖p_π − p_{π_j}‖ < 1/16 for some j. Put E_j := {x ∈ E : ‖p_{π_j} − p_{π_x}‖ < 1/16}; E = ⋃_jE_j.
7. Claim (10): for x ∈ E_j, X_{1/4}(π_j, x) ∩ E_j ∩ B_{δ/2}(x) = ∅. Otherwise pick y in it; y ≠ x and σ := |y − x| ∈ (0, δ/2). For z ∈ B_{σ/8}(y): dist(z − x, π_x) ≤ dist(y − x, π_x) + |z − y| ≤ dist(y − x, π_j) + ‖p_{π_j} − p_{π_x}‖σ + σ/8 < σ/4 + σ/16 + σ/8 = 7σ/16, while |z − x| > σ − σ/8 = 7σ/8; so dist(z − x, π_x) < |z − x|/2, and |z − x| < 9σ/8 < 2σ. Thus B_{σ/8}(y) ⊆ X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x). Since y, x ∈ E and σ/8, 2σ < δ, step 5 gives (1 − ε)ω_n(σ/8)ⁿ ≤ μ(B_{σ/8}(y)) ≤ μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x)) ≤ εω_n(2σ)ⁿ, i.e. 1 − ε ≤ 16ⁿε = 1/2, contradicting ε ≤ 1/32. (With Simon's printed ε = 16^{−n} the right side would be 1 and there would be no contradiction; this is the documented erratum.)
8. Lipschitz graphs. Fix j and x₀ ∈ ℝ^P and let D := E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀), p_j := p_{π_j^⊥} (projection onto the n-plane π_j^⊥). For x, y ∈ D, |x − y| < δ/2, so by (10) y ∉ X_{1/4}(π_j, x) unless y = x, i.e. |p_j(y − x)| = dist(y − x, π_j) ≥ |y − x|/4. Hence p_j is injective on D and h : p_j(D) → π_j, h(p_j x) := p_{π_j}x, is 4-Lipschitz. Extend h to a Lipschitz map h̃ : π_j^⊥ → π_j (coordinates in an orthonormal basis of π_j and McShane extension of each coordinate, Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.extend_real / LipschitzOnWith.extend_pi; constant ≤ 4√ℓ). With a linear isometry ι : ℝⁿ → π_j^⊥, F_{j,x₀}(u) := ι(u) + h̃(ι(u)) is Lipschitz and D ⊆ F_{j,x₀}(ℝⁿ) (x = p_jx + p_{π_j}x).
9. Finite cover. E is compact, so finitely many balls B_{δ/4}(x₀^{(s)}) cover it; the finitely many Lipschitz maps F_{j,x₀^{(s)}} cover ⋃_{j,s}(E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀^{(s)})) = E. Therefore μ(M ∖ ⋃_{j,s}F_{j,x₀^{(s)}}(ℝⁿ)) ≤ μ(M ∖ E) < ε'.
10. Conclusion. Applying steps 3–9 with ε' := 1/m for each m ≥ 1 yields countably many Lipschitz maps (F_k)_{k∈ℕ}, ℝⁿ → ℝ^P, such that M₀ := M ∖ ⋃_kF_k(ℝⁿ) satisfies Hⁿ(M₀) ≤ 1/m for all m, i.e. Hⁿ(M₀) = 0. Since M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_kF_k(ℝⁿ), M is countably n-rectifiable (definition CountablyRectifiable). ∎
proof_key_steps: Dispose of Hⁿ(M) = 0, n = 0, n > P and n = P.
At tangent points, μ = Hⁿ⌞M has density 1 and vanishing density in the cone X_{1/2}(Q(x)^⊥, x).
Lusin and Egorov give a compact E ⊆ M with μ(M∖E) < ε', continuous x ↦ Q(x) on E and uniform density estimates below δ.
With ε := 2^{−1}16^{−n} and a finite 1/16-net of ℓ-planes, the cone condition (10) holds on each E_j.
Hence each E_j ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) is a 4-Lipschitz graph over π_j^⊥, extendable to a Lipschitz map ℝⁿ → ℝ^P; finitely many cover E.
Taking ε' = 1/m for all m covers M by countably many Lipschitz images up to an Hⁿ-null set.

The corrected epsilon gives the cone contradiction; compact pieces admit Lipschitz graph extensions, and arbitrarily small discarded measure yields countable rectifiability. Degenerate dimensions are covered.

subproblem.title: Restricted representing integrals are determined by the represented current
subproblem.statement: Let P, k ∈ ℕ and U ⊆ ℝ^P open. For i = 1, 2, 3 let μ_i be a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ_i(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ξ_i : ℝ^P → Λ_k(ℝ^P) (MultiVector P k, continuous linear functionals on k-covectors) μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable with |ξ_i(x)(α)| ≤ |α| (Euclidean coefficient norm) for μ_i-a.e. x and every k-covector α. If ∫ ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫ ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫ ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃ for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), then for every Borel set B ⊆ ℝ^P and every ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U): ∫_B ξ₁(x)(ω(x)) dμ₁ = ∫_B ξ₂(x)(ω(x)) dμ₂ + ∫_B ξ₃(x)(ω(x)) dμ₃.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (μ₁ μ₂ μ₃ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ₁ ξ₂ ξ₃ : Euclid P → MultiVector P k), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ₁ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ₂ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ₃ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₁ μ₁ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₂ μ₂ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ₃ μ₃ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₁, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₁ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₂, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₂ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ₃, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ₃ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U k, ∫ x, ξ₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x, ξ₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₂ + ∫ x, ξ₃ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₃) → ∀ (B : Set (Euclid P)) (ω : TestFormOn U k), MeasurableSet B → ∫ x in B, ξ₁ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₁ = ∫ x in B, ξ₂ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₂ + ∫ x in B, ξ₃ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ₃
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the "Consequences" paragraph of the parent's (REP) notes and V4(o) of the parent proof (coordinatewise, a finite signed Radon measure annihilating C_c^∞ is zero). Notation: |α| is the Euclidean coefficient norm of a k-covector, ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)| for a test form ω, and ξ_i(ω) denotes x ↦ ξ_i(x)(ω(x)).

1. Integrability. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) and C := tsupport ω, a compact subset of U; ‖ω‖_∞ < ∞ since ω is continuous with compact support. For each i, x ↦ ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable (ξ_i is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable, ω is continuous and the evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) is continuous), and for μ_i-a.e. x, |ξ_i(x)(ω(x))| ≤ |ω(x)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ 1_C(x). Since μ_i(C) < ∞, ξ_i(ω) and ψ·ξ_i(ω) are μ_i-integrable for every bounded Borel ψ : ℝ^P → ℝ; in particular all integrals in the statement (over ℝ^P or over a Borel set B) are finite and well defined.

2. Coefficients. The space Λ^k of k-covectors on ℝ^P (Covector (Euclid P) k) is finite-dimensional. If it is {0} (this happens exactly when k > P, since an alternating k-linear map vanishes on k linearly dependent vectors, Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent) then ω = 0, all integrands vanish and the conclusion reads 0 = 0 + 0. Otherwise fix a basis (β_I)_{I ∈ ℐ} of Λ^k with dual coordinate functionals c_I (continuous linear maps Λ^k → ℝ). For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U) put ω_I := c_I ∘ ω; ω_I is C^∞ with tsupport ω_I ⊆ tsupport ω, a compact subset of U, and ω(x) = Σ_I ω_I(x) β_I. Put g_{i,I}(x) := ξ_i(x)(β_I); it is μ_i-a.e. strongly measurable with |g_{i,I}| ≤ |β_I| μ_i-a.e., and ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) g_{i,I}(x) by linearity of ξ_i(x). Replacing each g_{i,I} by a Borel function equal to it μ_i-a.e. (and bounded by |β_I|) changes none of the integrals below, so we may and do assume the g_{i,I} are Borel.

3. Test identities. For I ∈ ℐ and φ ∈ C_c^∞(U) (smooth, compact support inside U), the form φβ_I belongs to 𝒟^k(U), and the hypothesis applied to it gives
   ∫ φ g_{1,I} dμ₁ = ∫ φ g_{2,I} dμ₂ + ∫ φ g_{3,I} dμ₃.   (∗)

4. A signed measure. Fix I ∈ ℐ and ψ ∈ C_c^∞(U) and let S := tsupport ψ (compact ⊆ U). The functions h_i := ψ g_{i,I} are bounded by ‖ψ‖_∞|β_I| 1_S μ_i-a.e., so the two finite Borel measures
   ν₊ := (h₁)⁺μ₁ + (h₂)⁻μ₂ + (h₃)⁻μ₃,   ν₋ := (h₁)⁻μ₁ + (h₂)⁺μ₂ + (h₃)⁺μ₃
(withDensity measures; total masses ≤ ‖ψ‖_∞|β_I|(μ₁(S) + μ₂(S) + μ₃(S)) < ∞) satisfy ∫ φ dν₊ − ∫ φ dν₋ = ∫ φψ g_{1,I} dμ₁ − ∫ φψ g_{2,I} dμ₂ − ∫ φψ g_{3,I} dμ₃ for bounded Borel φ. For φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) the product φψ lies in C_c^∞(U), hence by (∗) ∫ φ dν₊ = ∫ φ dν₋ for all φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P).

5. Two finite Borel measures ν₊, ν₋ on ℝ^P with ∫ φ dν₊ = ∫ φ dν₋ for all φ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) are equal. (a) For φ ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) the mollifications φ_ε := φ ∗ ρ_ε are in C_c^∞(ℝ^P), satisfy |φ_ε| ≤ ‖φ‖_∞ and φ_ε → φ uniformly; dominated convergence for the finite measures ν_± gives ∫ φ dν₊ = ∫ φ dν₋. (b) For a compact set K choose φ_m ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with 0 ≤ φ_m ≤ 1, φ_m = 1 on K and φ_m = 0 outside {dist(·, K) < 1/m}; then φ_m ↓ 1_K pointwise and dominated convergence gives ν₊(K) = ν₋(K). (c) Compact sets form a π-system generating the Borel σ-algebra of ℝ^P (every closed set is a countable union of compact sets), and ν₊(ℝ^P) = lim_m ν₊(B̄_m(0)) = lim_m ν₋(B̄_m(0)) = ν₋(ℝ^P) < ∞; by uniqueness of finite measures agreeing on a generating π-system (Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite), ν₊ = ν₋.

6. Conclusion. Let B be Borel and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U). For each I apply steps 4–5 with ψ := ω_I and evaluate ν₊(B) = ν₋(B): ∫_B ω_I g_{1,I} dμ₁ = ∫_B ω_I g_{2,I} dμ₂ + ∫_B ω_I g_{3,I} dμ₃ (all integrals finite by step 1). Summing over the finitely many I ∈ ℐ and using ξ_i(x)(ω(x)) = Σ_I ω_I(x) g_{i,I}(x) (step 2) yields ∫_B ξ₁(ω) dμ₁ = ∫_B ξ₂(ω) dμ₂ + ∫_B ξ₃(ω) dμ₃. ∎
proof_key_steps: All integrands are integrable: |ξ_i(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞ 1_{tsupport ω} a.e. and μ_i(tsupport ω) < ∞.
Expand ω in a basis β_I of k-covectors: ξ_i(ω) = Σ_I ω_I g_{i,I} with g_{i,I} := ξ_i(β_I); the case Λ^k = 0 (k > P) is trivial.
Testing the hypothesis with φβ_I, φ ∈ C_c^∞(U), gives ∫φ g_{1,I}dμ₁ = ∫φ g_{2,I}dμ₂ + ∫φ g_{3,I}dμ₃.
For ψ ∈ C_c^∞(U) the finite measures ν_± built from the positive/negative parts of ψg_{i,I} have equal integrals against C_c^∞(ℝ^P).
Mollification, approximation of indicators of compact sets and uniqueness on the π-system of compact sets give ν₊ = ν₋.
Evaluate at B with ψ := ω_I and sum over I.

audit.reason: The proposition matches every representation and measurability hypothesis. Compact-support integrability, coefficient expansion, uniqueness of finite measures against smooth tests, and evaluation on Borel restrictions prove the exact conclusion without circularity.

subproblem.title: Integer multiplicity is a local property (T4) and passes to domain restrictions
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR) and (IMC). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; they are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. Let P, k ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open and X ∈ 𝒟_k(U). (1) If M_W(X) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and every x ∈ U has r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U such that the domain restriction X|_{B_r(x)} ∈ 𝒟_k(B_r(x)) (X.restrictDomain) is integer multiplicity, then X is integer multiplicity. (2) If V ⊆ U is open and X is integer multiplicity, then X|_V ∈ 𝒟_k(V) is integer multiplicity.

B)) ∧ (∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α)) → ∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (X : GeometricCurrentOn U k), IsOpen U → ((∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → CompactlyContained W U → X.massOn W < ∞) → (∀ x ∈ U, ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∃ h : ball x r ⊆ U, IsIntegerMultiplicity (X.restrictDomain h)) → IsIntegerMultiplicity X) ∧ (∀ (V : Set (Euclid P)) (h : V ⊆ U), IsOpen V → IsIntegerMultiplicity X → IsIntegerMultiplicity (X.restrictDomain h))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part I T4 ("IM is local"), with the local hypothesis phrased through domain restrictions X|_B := X.restrictDomain (B ⊆ U), and the converse restriction statement used in Parts IV.3, V2 and V4(ii). The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure and cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub (not available to this child otherwise, hence assumed); (IMC)(a)–(d) denote its four conjuncts. For an IMRep R = (M, θ, ξ) put R.measure := θHᵏ⌞M (contract IMRep.measure); then R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫ ξ(ω) dR.measure (integral against a measure with density). ξ(ω) denotes x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)).

If U = ∅ then 𝒟^k(U) = {0}, X = 0 and both parts hold with the IMRep with empty carrier (mult 0, orient 0; all fields vacuous). Part (2) is the same statement as the accepted DAG declaration dtc_restrictDomain_isIntegerMultiplicity (not imported here; its argument is the one below).

Part (2) (restriction).
1. Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep of X in U and V ⊆ U open. Since θ ≥ 1 on M, Hᵏ(M ∩ K) ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U.
2. Define R_V := (M ∩ V, θ, ξ). M ∩ V is Borel and ⊆ V; it is countably k-rectifiable as a subset of M (SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono); θ is measurable and positive on M ∩ V; for compact K ⊆ V, ∫_{M∩V∩K} θ dHᵏ ≤ ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ < ∞; ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞(M ∩ V) (restriction of Hᵏ⌞M). Orientation: by (IMC)(a) in U with M ∩ V ⊆ M (both Borel, ⊆ U, local finiteness from step 1), for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ V and every subspace Q, M ∩ V has approximate tangent space Q at x iff M does; together with the IMRep property of R this gives, for Hᵏ-a.e. x ∈ M ∩ V, a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k (M ∩ V) x Q and ξ(x) a unit orientation of Q.
3. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(V) (also an element of 𝒟^k(U)), X|_V(ω) = X(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ = ∫_{M∩V} θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ, because ω(x) = 0 for x ∉ tsupport ω ⊆ V. So R_V represents X|_V, which is IM.

Part (1) (local implies global).
4. X has locally finite mass, so (REP) gives μ_X, ξ_X with μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ_X(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, μ_X(G) = M_G(X) for all open G, ξ_X μ_X-a.e. strongly measurable, |ξ_X(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for all x, α, and X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U).
5. Local identification of measures. Fix x ∈ U, r > 0 with B_r(x) ⊆ U and an IMRep R_x = (M_x, θ_x, ξ_x) in B_r(x) of X|_{B_r(x)}. Put B' := B_{r/2}(x); its closure is a compact subset of B_r(x). For open G ⊆ B_r(x), the admissible forms for M_G(X) (forms in 𝒟^k(U), tsupport ⊆ G, pointwise norm ≤ 1) are exactly the admissible forms for M_G(X|_{B_r(x)}), with equal values; so M_G(X) = M_G(X|_{B_r(x)}) = R_x.measure(G) by (MR) applied in the open set B_r(x). Hence μ_X(G) = R_x.measure(G) for every open G ⊆ B_r(x). The measures μ_X⌞B' and R_x.measure⌞B' are finite (μ_X(B') ≤ μ_X(closure B') < ∞) and agree on all open sets (G ∩ B' is open ⊆ B_r(x)); open sets form a π-system generating the Borel sets, so μ_X⌞B' = R_x.measure⌞B' (Mathlib MeasureTheory.ext_of_generate_finite).
6. Local identification of orientations. Apply the sibling theorem cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq (child restrict_unique) in the open set B' with (μ₁, ξ₁) := (μ_X, ξ_X), (μ₂, ξ₂) := (R_x.measure, ξ_x), (μ₃, ξ₃) := (0, 0): both measures are finite on compact subsets of B'; ξ_x is a.e. strongly measurable for R_x.measure ≪ Hᵏ⌞M_x; |ξ_x(y)(α)| ≤ |α| for R_x.measure-a.e. y by (IMC)(d); and for ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B'), ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = X(ω) = X|_{B_r(x)}(ω) = R_x.action(ω) = ∫ ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure. Hence ∫_E ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = ∫_E ξ_x(ω) dR_x.measure for every Borel E and ω ∈ 𝒟^k(B'). Let ν := μ_X⌞B' = R_x.measure⌞B'. For a k-covector α, a compact K ⊆ B' and φ ∈ C_c^∞(B') with φ = 1 on K, taking ω := φα and E ⊆ K gives ∫_E (ξ_X(α) − ξ_x(α)) dν = 0 for all Borel E ⊆ K, so ξ_X(y)(α) = ξ_x(y)(α) for ν-a.e. y ∈ K. Exhausting B' by countably many compact sets and letting α run through a finite basis of k-covectors: ξ_X = ξ_x μ_X-a.e. on B'.
7. Gluing. U is second countable, so countably many balls B'_i := B_{r_i/2}(x_i) as in steps 5–6 cover U. Let A_i := B'_i ∖ ⋃_{l<i} B'_l (Borel, pairwise disjoint, ⋃_i A_i = U), and define M := ⋃_i (M_{x_i} ∩ A_i), θ(y) := θ_{x_i}(y) and ξ(y) := ξ_{x_i}(y) for y ∈ A_i, θ(y) := 0 and ξ(y) := 0 for y ∉ U.
8. IMRep fields. M is Borel and ⊆ U; M is countably k-rectifiable (each M_{x_i} ∩ A_i ⊆ M_{x_i}; SimonGMT CountablyRectifiable.mono and countablyRectifiable_iUnion); θ is Borel and ℕ-valued (countable measurable gluing) with θ ≥ 1 on M; for compact K ⊆ U, ∫_{M∩K} θ dHᵏ = Σ_i ∫_{M_{x_i}∩A_i∩K} θ_{x_i} dHᵏ = Σ_i R_{x_i}.measure(A_i ∩ K) = Σ_i μ_X(A_i ∩ K) = μ_X(K) < ∞ (step 5, A_i ⊆ B'_i); ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M because on each Borel piece M ∩ A_i it coincides with ξ_{x_i}, which is a.e. strongly measurable for Hᵏ⌞M_{x_i} (countable gluing of a.e. strongly measurable functions along a measurable partition). Orientation: fix i. For Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M_{x_i} there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt k M_{x_i} y Q and ξ_{x_i}(y) a unit orientation of Q (IMRep R_{x_i}). Apply (IMC)(a) in the open set B_{r_i}(x_i) to M_{x_i} ∩ A_i ⊆ M_{x_i}, and in U to M_{x_i} ∩ A_i ⊆ M (local finiteness: θ ≥ 1 on M and on M_{x_i}, and ∫_{M∩K}θ, ∫_{M_{x_i}∩K}θ_{x_i} < ∞ for compact K in the respective open sets): for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M ∩ A_i = M_{x_i} ∩ A_i the approximate tangent spaces of M_{x_i}, of M_{x_i} ∩ A_i and of M at y coincide. Hence for Hᵏ-a.e. y ∈ M, ξ(y) is a unit orientation of an approximate tangent space of M at y.
9. Representation. For ω ∈ 𝒟^k(U), using countable additivity of the (absolutely convergent) integral, μ_X(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, and steps 5–6 on A_i ⊆ B'_i:
   X(ω) = ∫ ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} ξ_X(ω) dμ_X = Σ_i ∫_{A_i} ξ_{x_i}(ω) dR_{x_i}.measure = Σ_i ∫_{M_{x_i}∩A_i} θ_{x_i} ξ_{x_i}(ω) dHᵏ = ∫_M θ ξ(ω) dHᵏ.
So (M, θ, ξ) is an IMRep in U representing X, and X is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: (2): intersect the carrier of an IMRep with V; tangent spaces are unchanged a.e. by (IMC)(a); the representing integral is unchanged since test forms of V vanish off V.
(1): take the (REP) representation (μ_X, ξ_X) of X.
On each ball, masses of X and of the local IM current agree on open subsets, so μ_X = θ_xHᵏ⌞M_x there by (MR) and uniqueness of finite measures on open sets.
restrict_unique and coordinatewise testing give ξ_X = ξ_x μ_X-a.e. on the ball.
Glue the local IMReps along a countable disjoint Borel partition subordinate to countably many balls; check all IMRep fields ((IMC)(a) for tangent spaces).
The glued IMRep represents X by countable additivity of ∫ξ_X(ω)dμ_X.

audit.reason: Both locality and domain restriction are proved with the stated prerequisites. Local measure and orientation identification justify the countable gluing; local integrability and tangent-space locality supply all IMRep fields. The restrict_unique dependency is sufficient and correctly directed.

For all P, d ∈ ℕ there is η₀ > 0 with the following property. A current Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) has the integer slice property (ISP) if for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y in ℝ^P (Borel measures finite on compact sets; a.e. strongly measurable fields of (d+1)- resp. d-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; Y(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂Y(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms) and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, every pair of currents A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B integer multiplicity. If C ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) has ∂C = 0 and ISP, μ is a Borel measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for compact K and μ(W) = M_W(C) for every open W, and ξ is a μ-a.e. strongly measurable field of (d+1)-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x and C(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ for every test form ω, then liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_{d+1}r^{d+1}) ≥ η₀ for μ-a.e. x (ω_{d+1} = unitBallVolume (d+1)).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, V5 (Simon Ch. 6, 8.2 (2)–(6), with the corrections noted in the parent: the lower density replaces Θ^{*n} < η, and the filling's support is controlled by the deformation theorem) and T3 (cone inequality). The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support. Sibling used: cbr_isoperimetric_filling (which needs only (DT)). ISP(C) is the integer slice property as in the statement (for all admissible representations of C and ∂C, every Lipschitz f and a.e. t, ∂A − B is IM for the restriction currents A, B). n := d + 1, ω_n := unitBallVolume n, Θ(x) := liminf_{r↓0} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_n rⁿ), ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|.

Constants. If n ≥ 2 let c ≥ 1 be the constant of cbr_isoperimetric_filling for (P, m := n − 2) and κ(η) := c(2c)^{1/(n−1)}(2n)^{n/(n−1)}(ηω_n)^{1/(n−1)}; if n = 1 let κ :≡ 0. Choose η₀ ∈ (0, 1/4) with κ(η₀) ≤ 1/2 and, if n ≥ 2, 4cnη₀ω_n ≤ 1 (possible since κ(η) → 0 as η ↓ 0). η₀ depends only on (P, d).

Step 0 (cone inequality, parent T3). Claim: if X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) has M(X) < ∞, ∂X = 0 and spt X ⊆ B̄_ϱ(x₀), then |X(ω)| ≤ ϱ M(X)‖dω‖_∞ for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P). Proof: for a smooth j-form γ (j ≥ 1) let (Kγ)(x) := ∫_0^1 s^{j−1} ι_{x−x₀}γ(x₀ + s(x − x₀)) ds (homotopy operator of the contraction h_s(x) = x₀ + s(x − x₀)); differentiation under the integral sign shows Kγ is smooth, and Cartan's formula dι_v + ι_v d = L_v for the radial field v(x) = x − x₀ gives dKγ + Kdγ = γ − h₀^#γ = γ (h₀ is constant and j ≥ 1). Since |ι_vβ| ≤ |v||β| for the Euclidean coefficient norms, |Kγ(x)| ≤ |x − x₀|‖γ‖_∞/j. Choose ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) equal to 1 on a neighbourhood of spt X (spt X is compact). By (VO), X(ω) = X(ζω) (tsupport((1 − ζ)ω) misses spt X), and X(ζω) = X(ζdKω) + X(ζKdω); further X(ζdKω) = X(d(ζKω)) − X(dζ ∧ Kω) = ∂X(ζKω) − 0 = 0 (VO again: dζ vanishes near spt X). Let (μ_X, ξ_X) be the (REP) representation of X (finite mass); μ_X is carried by spt X (μ_X(G) = M_G(X) = 0 for every open G disjoint from spt X, by (VO)). Hence |X(ω)| = |∫ ξ_X(ζKdω) dμ_X| ≤ ∫_{spt X} |Kdω| dμ_X ≤ ϱ‖dω‖_∞ μ_X(ℝ^P)/(n+1) ≤ ϱ M(X)‖dω‖_∞.

1. Measurability of Θ. For r > 0, x ↦ μ(B_r(x)) is lower semicontinuous (if x_m → x then 1_{B_r(x)} ≤ liminf 1_{B_r(x_m)}; Fatou), and r ↦ μ(B_r(x)) is left continuous (B_r = ⋃_{s<r} B_s); the quotient μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) is left continuous in r, so Θ(x) = lim_m inf_{r∈ℚ∩(0,1/m)} μ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) is Borel.
2. Reduction. A := {x : Θ(x) < η₀} is Borel; μ is a locally finite Borel measure on ℝ^P, hence inner regular by compact sets on Borel sets, so it suffices to prove μ(K') = 0 for compact K' ⊆ A. Fix such K', ε₀ ∈ (0, 1) and W := {x : dist(x, K') < ε₀} (bounded open, μ(W) < ∞).
3. Good radii. Let x₁ ∈ K' and 0 < δ < ε₀/(2 + 3√P). Since Θ(x₁) < η₀ there is s ∈ (0, δ) with F(s) < η₀ω_n sⁿ, F(ρ) := μ(B_ρ(x₁)). F and F^{1/n} are nondecreasing, hence differentiable a.e., and, with F(0) := μ(B_0(x₁)) = μ(∅) = 0 (so F is nondecreasing on [0, s]), ∫_0^s (F^{1/n})' ≤ F(s)^{1/n} − F(0)^{1/n} = F(s)^{1/n} < (η₀ω_n)^{1/n}s (Mathlib MonotoneOn.intervalIntegral_deriv_mem_uIcc). Hence the set of ρ ∈ (0, s) with (F^{1/n})'(ρ) ≤ 2(η₀ω_n)^{1/n} has positive measure. Remove the null sets where F or F^{1/n} is not differentiable, the countable set {ρ : μ(∂B_ρ(x₁)) > 0} (μ is σ-finite), and the null set of ρ where the ISP conclusion fails for f := |· − x₁| (1-Lipschitz) with the admissible representations (μ, ξ) of C and (0, 0) of ∂C = 0. Choose ρ in the remaining (non-empty) set.
4. The slice. (SL) with k := n − 1, T := C, (μ, ξ), (0, 0), f := |· − x₁|, L := 1 gives currents A_ρ with A_ρ(ω) = ∫_{B_ρ(x₁)} ξ(ω) dμ =: (C⌞B_ρ(x₁))(ω), B_ρ = 0, and Z := ∂A_ρ with Z(η) = 0 whenever tsupport η ∩ ∂B_ρ(x₁) = ∅ (so spt Z ⊆ ∂B_ρ(x₁), compact) and M(Z) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ({ρ − h < |· − x₁| < ρ}) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹(F(ρ) − F(ρ − h)) = F'(ρ). By the choice of ρ, Z = ∂A_ρ − 0 is IM; if n ≥ 2, ∂Z = ∂∂A_ρ = 0.
5. Mass bound. As F = (F^{1/n})ⁿ with both differentiable at ρ, F'(ρ) = nF(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}(F^{1/n})'(ρ) ≤ 2n(η₀ω_n)^{1/n}F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}; with F(ρ) ≤ F(s) < η₀ω_nsⁿ this gives M(Z) ≤ 2nη₀ω_n s^{n−1}, and also M(Z)^{n/(n−1)} ≤ (2n)^{n/(n−1)}(η₀ω_n)^{1/(n−1)}F(ρ) when n ≥ 2.
6. Filling. If n ≥ 2: cbr_isoperimetric_filling (m := n − 2; Z IM, spt Z compact, ∂Z = 0, M(Z) < ∞) gives an IM S ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂S = Z, M(S) ≤ c(2cM(Z))^{1/(n−1)}M(Z) = c(2c)^{1/(n−1)}M(Z)^{n/(n−1)} ≤ κ(η₀)F(ρ) = κ(η₀)μ(B_ρ(x₁)), and spt S ⊆ thickening(3√P(2cM(Z))^{1/(n−1)}, ∂B_ρ(x₁)) ⊆ B̄_{ρ + 3√P(4cnη₀ω_n)^{1/(n−1)}s}(x₁) ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁) (since 2cM(Z) ≤ 4cnη₀ω_n s^{n−1}, 4cnη₀ω_n ≤ 1 and ρ < s < δ). If n = 1: M(Z) ≤ 2η₀ω_1 = 4η₀ < 1; Z is an IM 0-current and by (MR) its mass equals Σ_{x∈carrier} mult(x) (H⁰ is the counting measure), which is ≥ 1 unless the carrier is empty; so the carrier is empty, Z = 0, and S := 0 satisfies ∂S = Z, M(S) = 0 = κμ(B_ρ(x₁)) and spt S = ∅.
7. Covering. For fixed δ and x₁ ∈ K' let 𝓡_δ(x₁) be the set of radii ρ ∈ (0, δ) that arise as in step 3 for some s ∈ (ρ, δ) with F(s) < η₀ω_nsⁿ (and satisfy all the requirements of steps 3–6); applying step 3 with δ replaced by any δ'' ∈ (0, δ) shows that 𝓡_δ(x₁) contains arbitrarily small radii, so the closed balls B̄_ρ(x₁), ρ ∈ 𝓡_δ(x₁), form a fine family at every point of K'. By the Besicovitch–Vitali covering theorem (Mathlib Besicovitch.exists_disjoint_closedBall_covering_ae, for the locally finite measure μ) there are countably many pairwise disjoint balls B_i = B̄_{ρ_i}(x_i) of this family with μ(K' ∖ ⋃_i B_i) = 0; B_i ⊆ W since ρ_i < δ < ε₀. Let S_i be the fillings of step 6 and C_i(ω) := ∫_{B_i} ξ(ω) dμ = A_{ρ_i}(ω) (μ(∂B_{ρ_i}(x_i)) = 0). Then X_i := S_i − C_i has ∂X_i = Z_i − Z_i = 0, M(X_i) ≤ M(S_i) + μ(B_i) ≤ (1 + κ)μ(B_i), and spt X_i ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x_i).
8. Comparison currents. Step 0 with ϱ := (1 + 3√P)δ gives |X_i(ω)| ≤ (1 + 3√P)δ(1 + κ)μ(B_i)‖dω‖_∞. The B_i are disjoint subsets of W, so Σ_iμ(B_i) ≤ μ(W) < ∞. For a Borel set E, C⌞E(ω) := ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ is a current (linear; |C⌞E(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞μ(tsupport ω) gives sequential continuity) with M_{W'}(C⌞E) ≤ μ(W' ∩ E) for open W'. The series ω ↦ Σ_iS_i(ω) converges absolutely (|S_i(ω)| ≤ κμ(B_i)‖ω‖_∞) and defines a current Σ_iS_i (the partial sums are uniformly bounded by κμ(W)‖ω‖_∞), with M(Σ_iS_i) ≤ Σ_iM(S_i) ≤ κμ(W). With E := ℝ^P ∖ ⋃_iB_i, countable additivity of the integral gives C = C⌞E + Σ_iC_i, hence C_δ := C⌞E + Σ_iS_i = C + Σ_iX_i and |C_δ(ω) − C(ω)| ≤ (1 + 3√P)δ(1 + κ)μ(W)‖dω‖_∞.
9. Lower semicontinuity. Along δ = δ_m ↓ 0 we get C_{δ_m} ⇀ C, so by SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf, μ(W) = M_W(C) ≤ liminf_m M_W(C_{δ_m}) ≤ liminf_m (μ(W ∖ ⋃_iB_i^{(m)}) + Σ_iM(S_i^{(m)})) ≤ μ(W ∖ K') + κ(η₀)μ(W), using μ(W ∖ ⋃_iB_i) ≤ μ(W ∖ K') + μ(K' ∖ ⋃_iB_i) = μ(W ∖ K') and Σ_iM(S_i) ≤ κΣ_iμ(B_i) ≤ κμ(W).
10. Since κ(η₀) ≤ 1/2 and μ(W) < ∞: μ(W) ≤ 2μ(W ∖ K'), i.e. μ(K') ≤ μ({dist(·, K') < ε₀} ∖ K'). As ε₀ ↓ 0 these sets decrease to ∅ (K' is closed) and have finite measure, so μ(K') = 0. Hence μ(A) = 0, i.e. ENNReal.ofReal η₀ ≤ Θ(x) for μ-a.e. x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Cone inequality: a finite-mass cycle supported in B̄_ϱ(x₀) satisfies |X(ω)| ≤ ϱM(X)‖dω‖_∞ (homotopy operator, (VO), (REP)).
The lower density is Borel; by inner regularity it suffices to show μ(K') = 0 for compact K' in the low-density set.
At x₁ ∈ K' choose radii ρ with F'(ρ) ≤ 2n(η₀ω_n)^{1/n}F(ρ)^{(n−1)/n}, μ(∂B_ρ) = 0 and IM slice Z = ∂(C⌞B_ρ(x₁)) with M(Z) ≤ F'(ρ) ((SL), ISP).
Fill Z by isoperimetric (n ≥ 2) with M(S) ≤ κ(η₀)μ(B_ρ(x₁)) and spt S ⊆ B̄_{(1+3√P)δ}(x₁); for n = 1, Z = 0 by (MR).
Besicovitch–Vitali gives disjoint balls covering μ-almost all of K'; the cone inequality shows C⌞(ℝ^P∖⋃B_i) + ΣS_i ⇀ C as δ ↓ 0.
Lower semicontinuity of M_W gives μ(W) ≤ μ(W∖K') + κμ(W) ≤ μ(W∖K') + μ(W)/2, hence μ(K') = 0.

audit.reason: The proof establishes the stated uniform positive lower-density bound. Good radii, controlled fillings, the degree-one mass gap, disjoint covering, cone estimates, and lower semicontinuity give the required contradiction on every compact low-density subset. No closure conclusion is assumed.

subproblem.title: Boundary rectifiability BR(d) from the closure theorem CL(d) (Simon 6.3 via the deformation theorem)
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT) and (VO). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; they are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. CL(d) denotes: for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), T is integer multiplicity; BR(d) denotes: for all P, open U and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every such W, ∂R is integer multiplicity. Then for every d ∈ ℕ, CL(d) implies BR(d).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part IV (BR(d) from CL(d); Simon Ch. 6, 6.2–6.3). The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; CL(d) is the closure statement in degree d (for all P, open U, IM T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for open W ⊂⊂ U and T_j ⇀ T: T is IM). Siblings used: cbr_measure_convergence_tools (part (MM)) and cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (parts (1), (2)). ‖ω‖_∞ := sup_x |ω(x)|; ξ(ω) := x ↦ ξ(x)(ω(x)).

0. General facts. (i) For a current X in an open set V with finite mass and ω ∈ 𝒟(V): |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖_∞ (if ω ≠ 0, ±ω/‖ω‖_∞ are admissible for the mass, the norm being even). (ii) Masses are subadditive: M_W(X − Y) ≤ M_W(X) + M_W(Y) and M_W(0 − Y) = M_W(Y). (iii) If (μ, ξ) is an admissible representation of X then M_W(X) ≤ μ(W) for open W. (iv) The zero current is IM: the IMRep with empty carrier, mult 0 and orient 0 (∅ is Borel and countably rectifiable, SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_of_measure_zero; all other fields are vacuous since Hᵈ⌞∅ = 0; the integral over ∅ is 0). If d + 1 > P, every (d+1)-covector on ℝ^P vanishes (Mathlib AlternatingMap.map_linearDependent), so R = 0 and ∂R(η) = R(dη) = 0, and ∂R = 0 is IM by (iv). The argument below does not need d + 1 ≤ P.
1. Representations. Let R be IM with IMRep (M, θ, ξ) in U; μ := θH^{d+1}⌞M (contract IMRep.measure), finite on compact subsets of U (local integrability of θ); ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (μ ≪ H^{d+1}⌞M) and |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for μ-a.e. x by (IMC)(d); R(ω) = ∫ ξ(ω) dμ. ∂R has locally finite mass by hypothesis, so (REP) gives μ', ξ' with μ'(K) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U, |ξ'| ≤ 1 everywhere, ξ' μ'-a.e. strongly measurable and ∂R(η) = ∫ ξ'(η) dμ'.
2. Slicing. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U; f := |· − x₀| (1-Lipschitz), G := B_{r₀}(x₀). (SL) with k := d, T := R, (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ'), f, L := 1 gives currents A_t ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), B_t ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ', such that Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t satisfies Z_t(η) = 0 whenever tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅, and M_G(Z_t) ≤ liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹ μ(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}).
3. Good radius. Apply (MM) of cbr_measure_convergence_tools to the constant sequence μ_j := μ with G, (a, b) := (0, r₀), L := 1, Z_j(t) := M_G(Z_t): μ(G ∩ {0 < f < r₀}) ≤ μ(B̄_{r₀}(x₀)) < ∞, so the measurable majorant g has ∫⁻_{(0,r₀)} g < ∞; hence g < ∞ a.e. and M_G(Z_r) < ∞ for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀). Fix such r.
4. Total mass of Z_r. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^d(U) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in G and χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the sphere {f = r} (compact, ⊆ G as r < r₀). Then tsupport((1 − χ)ω) ∩ {f = r} = ∅, so Z_r((1 − χ)ω) = 0 and Z_r(ω) = Z_r(χω) ≤ M_G(Z_r) (χω is admissible for M_G). Hence M(Z_r) = M_U(Z_r) ≤ M_G(Z_r) < ∞.
5. R' := A_r = R⌞B_r(x₀). By (IMC)(b) with E := B_r(x₀) = {f < r} there are a current A' and an IMRep R'' = (M ∩ B_r(x₀), θ, ξ) of A'; A'(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_r(x₀)} θ ξ(ω) dH^{d+1} = ∫_{f<r} ξ(ω) dμ = A_r(ω), so R' = A_r = A' is IM, with carrier inside B_r(x₀). If tsupport ω ∩ B̄_r(x₀) = ∅ then R'(ω) = 0, so spt R' ⊆ B̄_r(x₀). M(R') ≤ μ(B_r(x₀)) < ∞ by 0(iii) (or by (MR)). ∂R' = B_r + Z_r with M(B_r) ≤ μ'(B_r(x₀)) ≤ μ'(B̄_{r₀}(x₀)) < ∞ (0(iii) for the admissible representation (μ'⌞{f<r}, ξ') of B_r), hence M(∂R') ≤ M(B_r) + M(Z_r) < ∞.
6. Extension to ℝ^P. Fix ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of B̄_r(x₀). Define R̂'(ω) := R'(ζω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P) (ζω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U)). R̂' is linear and sequentially continuous (multiplication by ζ maps test-form-convergent sequences in ℝ^P to test-form-convergent sequences supported in tsupport ζ ⊆ U), so R̂' ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P). Since ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀) ⊇ carrier of R'', R̂'(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_r(x₀)} θ ξ(ζω) dH^{d+1} = ∫_{M∩B_r(x₀)} θ ξ(ω) dH^{d+1}, and R'' is also an IMRep in ℝ^P (its carrier is a Borel subset of ℝ^P, ∫_{M∩B_r(x₀)∩K} θ ≤ μ(B̄_r(x₀)) < ∞ for every compact K, the other fields are unchanged); so R̂' is IM. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(U), tsupport((1 − ζ)ω) is disjoint from spt R' ⊆ B̄_r(x₀), so R̂'(ω) = R'(ω) by (VO). Consequently M(R̂') = M(R') (≤: ζω is admissible when ω is, since 0 ≤ ζ ≤ 1; ≥: admissible forms of U are admissible forms of ℝ^P with the same value) and spt R̂' ⊆ B̄_r(x₀) (if tsupport ω ∩ B̄_r(x₀) = ∅ then R̂'(ω) = ∫_{M∩B_r} θ ξ(ω) = 0, and every point outside B̄_r(x₀) has a ball with compact closure in this zero region). Boundary: for η ∈ 𝒟^d(ℝ^P), ∂R̂'(η) = R'(ζ dη) and ∂R'(ζη) = R'(d(ζη)); the forms ζdη and d(ζη) coincide on the open set N where ζ ≡ 1 (a neighbourhood of B̄_r(x₀) containing the carrier M ∩ B_r(x₀) of R''), so integrating against R'' gives R'(ζdη) = R'(d(ζη)), i.e. ∂R̂'(η) = ∂R'(ζη). (Equivalently: d(ζη) = dζ ∧ η + ζdη and R'(dζ ∧ η) = 0 by (VO), dζ vanishing near B̄_r(x₀) ⊇ spt R'.) Hence M(∂R̂') ≤ M(∂R') < ∞ (|ζη| ≤ |η|).
7. Deformation. Let c ≥ 1 be the constant of (DT) for (P, m := d), K := B̄_r(x₀) (compact) and Λ := M(R̂') (finite; taken in ℝ≥0). For each k ∈ ℕ let ρ_k := 2^{−k}; (DT) applied to T := R̂' (IM, spt ⊆ K, M(R̂') ≤ Λ, M(∂R̂') < ∞) gives Q_k, S_k ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) and R_k ∈ 𝒟_{d+2}(ℝ^P) with Q_k and ∂Q_k IM, R̂' − Q_k − S_k = ∂R_k, M(∂Q_k) ≤ c M(∂R̂'), M(R_k) ≤ cρ_k M(R̂') and M(S_k) ≤ cρ_k M(∂R̂').
8. Convergence. For ω ∈ 𝒟^{d+1}(ℝ^P): R̂'(ω) − Q_k(ω) = S_k(ω) + R_k(dω), so by 0(i) |R̂'(ω) − Q_k(ω)| ≤ M(S_k)‖ω‖_∞ + M(R_k)‖dω‖_∞ ≤ cρ_k(M(∂R̂')‖ω‖_∞ + M(R̂')‖dω‖_∞) → 0. Thus Q_k ⇀ R̂' and, by SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary, ∂Q_k ⇀ ∂R̂'.
9. Closure in degree d. Apply CL(d) with P, U := ℝ^P (open), T_k := ∂Q_k (IM) and T := ∂R̂': for every open W, M_W(∂Q_k) ≤ M(∂Q_k) ≤ cM(∂R̂') < ∞ and boundaryMassOn(∂Q_k, W) = 0 (if d = 0 by definition; if d ≥ 1 it equals M_W(∂∂Q_k) = M_W(0) = 0 by SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary). Hence ∂R̂' is IM.
10. Back to ∂R. Let η ∈ 𝒟^d(B_r(x₀)), viewed in 𝒟^d(U) and 𝒟^d(ℝ^P). Then ζη = η, so ∂R̂'(η) = ∂R'(η) = B_r(η) + Z_r(η); Z_r(η) = 0 since tsupport η ⊆ B_r(x₀) misses {f = r}; and B_r(η) = ∫_{f<r} ξ'(η) dμ' = ∫ ξ'(η) dμ' = ∂R(η) because η vanishes off B_r(x₀) = {f < r}. Hence the domain restrictions agree: (∂R)|_{B_r(x₀)} = (∂R̂')|_{B_r(x₀)}, and the latter is IM by part (2) of cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (in the open set ℝ^P, with V := B_r(x₀)).
11. Steps 2–10 work for every x₀ ∈ U (with r = r(x₀) > 0 and B_r(x₀) ⊆ U), and ∂R has locally finite mass by hypothesis; by part (1) of cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local, ∂R is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Represent R by its IMRep and ∂R by (REP); slice by f = |· − x₀| with (SL).
By (MM), for a.e. r the slice Z_r has finite mass in B_{r₀}(x₀), hence finite total mass.
R' := R⌞B_r(x₀) is IM ((IMC)(b)), compactly supported, with ∂R' = (∂R)⌞B_r + Z_r of finite mass; extend R' to ℝ^P by a cutoff ((VO)).
The deformation theorem with ρ_k = 2^{−k} gives IM Q_k with IM boundaries, Q_k ⇀ R̂' and bounded M(∂Q_k).
CL(d) in ℝ^P shows ∂R̂' is IM.
∂R̂' agrees with ∂R on B_r(x₀); im_local (2) then (1) shows ∂R is IM.

audit.reason: Localization and deformation produce IM d-boundaries with uniformly bounded masses and zero boundary mass. CL(d), followed by domain restriction and locality, proves BR(d) without invoking CL(d+1). This agrees with the lower-dimensional use in [Simon, Chapter 6, §§6.2–6.4](https://math.stanford.edu/~lms/ntu-gmt-text.pdf).

For every P, every open U ⊆ ℝ^P and T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_0(U): if every T_j is integer multiplicity, sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U (the boundary term is 0 in degree 0), and T_j ⇀ T in U, then T is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part III (CL(0)), with the final appeal to T4 made through the sibling theorem cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (child im_local), whose hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC) (the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub; not available to this child, hence assumed) are hypotheses here. For a 0-covector α write ⟨α⟩ := α(∅) (the value on the empty tuple); α ↦ ⟨α⟩ identifies Covector(ℝ^P, 0) with ℝ, and |α| = |⟨α⟩|. A 0-form a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) is identified with the smooth function x ↦ ⟨a(x)⟩.

1. Degree-0 IMReps. H⁰ = μHE[0] = μH[0] (Mathlib MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero) is the counting measure (μH[0]{x} = 1, Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton). Let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an IMRep in U of S ∈ 𝒟_0(U). (i) For compact K ⊆ U, Σ_{x∈M∩K} θ(x) = ∫_{M∩K} θ dH⁰ < ∞ and θ ≥ 1 on M, so M ∩ K is finite. (ii) The only H⁰-null subset of M is ∅, so the orientation property of R holds at every x ∈ M: ξ(x) is a unit orientation of a 0-dimensional subspace; by the definition IsUnitOrientationOf with n = 0 (the orthonormal family is the empty family) ξ(x)(α) = ε(x)⟨α⟩ with ε(x) ∈ {1, −1}. (iii) Hence, with m(x) := ε(x)θ(x) ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}, S(a) = Σ_{x∈M} m(x)⟨a(x)⟩ for a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) (a finite sum: only x ∈ M ∩ tsupport a contribute). (iv) By (MR), for open G, M_G(S) = R.measure(G) = Σ_{x∈M∩G} θ(x) = Σ_{x∈M∩G} |m(x)|.
2. Locally finite mass of T. For open W ⊂⊂ U, M_W(T) ≤ liminf_j M_W(T_j) (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) ≤ sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ (boundaryMassOn is 0 in degree 0, and M_W(T_j) is bounded by the hypothesis).
3. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r > 0 with B̄_{2r}(x₀) ⊆ U. The open set B_{2r}(x₀) has compact closure in U, so c := sup_j M_{B_{2r}(x₀)}(T_j) < ∞. Let R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) be IMReps of T_j and m_j as in step 1. By 1(iv), Σ_{x∈M_j∩B_{2r}(x₀)} |m_j(x)| ≤ c. Listing each x ∈ M_j ∩ B_{2r}(x₀) exactly |m_j(x)| times with sign ε_j(x): T_j(a) = Σ_{i=1}^{N_j} ε_{j,i}⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ for all a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport a ⊆ B_{2r}(x₀), where N_j ≤ c, ε_{j,i} ∈ {±1} and x_{j,i} ∈ B_{2r}(x₀).
4. N_j takes values in the finite set {0, …, ⌊c⌋} and (ε_{j,1}, …, ε_{j,N}) in the finite set {±1}^N, and B̄_{2r}(x₀)^N is compact; hence there is a subsequence (not relabeled; it still converges weakly to T) with N_j = N, ε_{j,i} = ε_i and x_{j,i} → y_i ∈ B̄_{2r}(x₀) for i = 1, …, N.
5. For a ∈ 𝒟^0(U) with tsupport a ⊆ B_r(x₀): T(a) = lim_j T_j(a) = lim_j Σ_{i=1}^N ε_i⟨a(x_{j,i})⟩ = Σ_{i=1}^N ε_i⟨a(y_i)⟩ (a continuous). Let Y := {y_1, …, y_N}, m(y) := Σ_{i: y_i = y} ε_i ∈ ℤ for y ∈ Y and F := {y ∈ Y ∩ B_r(x₀) : m(y) ≠ 0}, a finite subset of B_r(x₀). Since a vanishes on Y ∖ B_r(x₀) (outside tsupport a), T(a) = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩.
6. The domain restriction T|_{B_r(x₀)} ∈ 𝒟_0(B_r(x₀)) is integer multiplicity. Define an IMRep in B_r(x₀): carrier F; mult(y) := |m(y)| for y ∈ F, 0 otherwise; orient(y)(α) := sign(m(y))⟨α⟩ for y ∈ F, orient(y) := 0 otherwise. F is finite, hence Borel; it is countably 0-rectifiable (each point is the range of a constant, hence Lipschitz, map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P; SimonGMT countablyRectifiable_range and countablyRectifiable_iUnion); mult and orient take finitely many values on finitely many points, so they are Borel/strongly measurable; mult > 0 on F; ∫_{F∩K} mult dH⁰ ≤ Σ_{y∈F}|m(y)| < ∞. Orientation at y ∈ F: the subspace {0} has finrank 0 and, with δ := dist(y, F ∖ {y}) > 0 (δ := ∞ if F = {y}), for f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P) with tsupport f ⊆ B_{R_f}(0) and 0 < ρ < δ/R_f, the blow-up blowUpMap y ρ (F) = ρ⁻¹(F − y) meets tsupport f at most in 0, so ∫_{blowUpMap y ρ '' F} f dH⁰ = f(0) = ∫_{{0}} f dH⁰; thus HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 0 F y {0}, and orient(y) = ±⟨·⟩ is a unit orientation of {0} (IsUnitOrientationOf with the empty orthonormal family). Representation: for a ∈ 𝒟^0(B_r(x₀)), the action is Σ_{y∈F} |m(y)| sign(m(y))⟨a(y)⟩ = Σ_{y∈F} m(y)⟨a(y)⟩ = T(a) = T|_{B_r(x₀)}(a) by step 5.
7. Steps 3–6 apply to every x₀ ∈ U (with some r > 0, B_r(x₀) ⊆ U). Together with step 2, part (1) of the sibling theorem cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (applied with the hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC)) shows that T is integer multiplicity. ∎
proof_key_steps: Degree-0 IMReps are locally finite point sets with integer weights m(x) ≠ 0 (H⁰ is counting measure, orientations ±1), and by (MR) M_G = Σ|m| on open G.
T has locally finite mass by lower semicontinuity.
On B_{2r}(x₀) each T_j is a sum of at most c signed Dirac masses; pass to a subsequence with constant count and signs and convergent points.
On B_r(x₀), T equals a finite integer combination of Dirac masses, which is IM (explicit IMRep, approximate tangent space {0}).
Conclude with part (1) of im_local.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, V4(ii) ("(ISP) passes to weak limits"). The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub and cmc_slice_mass_bounds; CL(d) is the closure statement in degree d. Siblings used: cbr_measure_convergence_tools (parts (T1), (T2), (MM)) and cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local. ISP(Y), for Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), is the integer slice property of the statement: for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y in ℝ^P (measures finite on compact sets, a.e. strongly measurable fields bounded by 1 a.e., representing Y and ∂Y on all test forms) and every Lipschitz f, for a.e. t ∈ ℝ, every pair A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B integer multiplicity. W_k := B_{k+1}(0).

1. Locally finite masses. For bounded open W (i.e. W ⊂⊂ ℝ^P), Λ_W := sup_i (M_W(X_i) + M_W(∂X_i)) < ∞. By SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf and WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary (∂X_i ⇀ ∂X), M_W(X) ≤ Λ_W and M_W(∂X) ≤ Λ_W.
2. Fix admissible representations (μ, ξ) of X and (μ', ξ') of ∂X and an L-Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ (continuous). We must find a null set N ⊆ ℝ such that for t ∉ N and all currents A, B with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, B(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η) dμ', the current ∂A − B is IM.
3. Mass representations of X_i, ∂X_i. By (REP) in U := ℝ^P (locally finite masses), there are (μ_i, ξ_i) for X_i and (μ'_i, ξ'_i) for ∂X_i with μ_i(W) = M_W(X_i), μ'_i(W) = M_W(∂X_i) for open W, fields bounded by 1 everywhere and a.e. strongly measurable, representing X_i and ∂X_i. For compact K, choosing a bounded open W ⊇ K, sup_i μ_i(K) ≤ Λ_W and sup_i μ'_i(K) ≤ Λ_W.
4. Limit measures. By (T1) with U := ℝ^P applied to (μ_i), and then to (μ'_i) along the resulting subsequence, there are a subsequence (not relabeled; it still converges weakly to X, keeps the mass bounds, and its members still have ISP) and Borel measures ν, ν', finite on compact sets, with limsup_i μ_i(K) ≤ ν(K) and limsup_i μ'_i(K) ≤ ν'(K) for all compact K (a further subsequence of a sequence with this property keeps it).
5. Slices of X_i. For each i, (SL) (k := d) applied to X_i with (μ_i, ξ_i), (μ'_i, ξ'_i), f, L gives currents A_{i,t}, B_{i,t} with A_{i,t}(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ_i(ω) dμ_i, B_{i,t}(η) = ∫_{f<t} ξ'_i(η) dμ'_i, and Z_{i,t} := ∂A_{i,t} − B_{i,t} satisfies M_W(Z_{i,t}) ≤ L liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ_i(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open W. If d ≥ 1, write d = d' + 1 and apply (SL) also to ∂X_i ∈ 𝒟_{d'+1}(ℝ^P) with the representations (μ'_i, ξ'_i) of ∂X_i and (0, 0) of ∂∂X_i = 0 (admissible: the zero measure); its first family has the same values as B_{i,t}, hence equals B_{i,t} (currents are determined by their values), and its second family is 0, so M_W(∂B_{i,t}) ≤ L liminf_{h↓0} h⁻¹μ'_i(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}). If d = 0 put the second majorant equal to 0.
6. ISP of X_i, instantiated with (μ_i, ξ_i), (μ'_i, ξ'_i) and f, gives null sets N_i such that Z_{i,t} is IM for t ∉ N_i.
7. Good parameters. For k, m ∈ ℕ apply (MM) with μs i := μ_i + μ'_i, G := W_k, (a, b) := (−m, m), the given L and Z_i(t) := M_{W_k}(Z_{i,t}) + M_{W_k}(∂B_{i,t}) (≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹(μ_i + μ'_i)(W_k ∩ {t − h < f < t}) because liminf u_h + liminf v_h ≤ liminf (u_h + v_h)); finiteness: (μ_i + μ'_i)(W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}) ≤ M_{W_k}(X_i) + M_{W_k}(∂X_i) ≤ Λ_{W_k}. The measurable majorant g_{k,m} has ∫⁻ g_{k,m} ≤ LΛ_{W_k} < ∞, so for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m): liminf_i (M_{W_k}(Z_{i,t}) + M_{W_k}(∂B_{i,t})) < ∞. The sets {t : ν{f = t} > 0} and {t : ν'{f = t} > 0} are countable: ν, ν' are finite on compact sets, hence locally finite and (ℝ^P being σ-compact) σ-finite, so Mathlib countable_meas_level_set_pos applies to the disjoint measurable level sets {f = t}. Let N be the union of all these exceptional null sets (over k, m), of the N_i, and of these two countable sets: N is null. Fix t ∉ N and A, B as in step 2.
8. Convergence of the slices. (T2) applied to X_i ⇀ X with the representations (μ_i, ξ_i), the target representation (μ, ξ), the limit measure ν (limsup property of step 4, ν{f = t} = 0) and the continuous f gives ∫_{f<t} ξ_i(ω) dμ_i → ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, i.e. A_{i,t}(ω) → A(ω) for every ω. (T2) applied to ∂X_i ⇀ ∂X with (μ'_i, ξ'_i), (μ', ξ'), ν' gives B_{i,t}(η) → B(η). Hence Z_{i,t}(η) = A_{i,t}(dη) − B_{i,t}(η) → A(dη) − B(η) = (∂A − B)(η) for every η: Z_{i,t} ⇀ Z := ∂A − B. This holds along every further subsequence.
9. Closure on W_k. Fix k. By step 7 choose a further subsequence (i_l) (depending on k and t) with Σ_k := sup_l (M_{W_k}(Z_{i_l,t}) + M_{W_k}(∂B_{i_l,t})) < ∞. If d ≥ 1, ∂Z_{i,t} = ∂∂A_{i,t} − ∂B_{i,t} = −∂B_{i,t}, so M_{W_k}(∂Z_{i_l,t}) ≤ Σ_k. The domain restrictions Z_{i_l,t}|_{W_k} ∈ 𝒟_d(W_k) are IM (step 6 and part (2) of cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local in ℝ^P), converge weakly in W_k to Z|_{W_k} (step 8; test forms of W_k are test forms of ℝ^P), and for open W'' ⊂⊂ W_k: M_{W''}(Z_{i_l,t}|_{W_k}) = M_{W''}(Z_{i_l,t}) ≤ Σ_k (the admissible forms coincide) and boundaryMassOn(Z_{i_l,t}|_{W_k}, W'') is 0 if d = 0 and equals M_{W''}(∂Z_{i_l,t}) ≤ Σ_k if d ≥ 1 (domain restriction commutes with the boundary). By CL(d) in the open set W_k, Z|_{W_k} is IM.
10. Locally finite mass of Z. For bounded open W pick k with W ⊆ W_k; by lower semicontinuity along (i_l), M_W(Z) ≤ liminf_l M_W(Z_{i_l,t}) ≤ Σ_k < ∞.
11. Conclusion. For x ∈ ℝ^P pick k > |x|; then B_1(x) ⊆ W_k and Z|_{B_1(x)} = (Z|_{W_k})|_{B_1(x)} is IM by part (2) of cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local in W_k. By part (1) of the same theorem (U := ℝ^P, locally finite mass from step 10), Z = ∂A − B is IM. Since t ∉ N and A, B were arbitrary, X has ISP. ∎
proof_key_steps: X, ∂X have locally finite mass; fix admissible representations of X, ∂X and a Lipschitz f.
Take (REP) mass representations of X_i, ∂X_i and, by (T1), a subsequence with limit measures ν, ν'.
Slice X_i (and ∂X_i if d ≥ 1) with (SL); ISP of X_i makes the slices IM for a.e. t.
(MM) for the summed majorants on B_{k+1}(0) and (−m, m) gives, for a.e. t, finite liminf of slice masses and slice-boundary masses; also ν{f=t} = ν'{f=t} = 0.
(T2) for X_i and ∂X_i gives slice convergence to ∂A − B.
Along a bounded subsequence, CL(d) in B_{k+1}(0) makes (∂A − B)|_{B_{k+1}(0)} IM.
Lower semicontinuity gives locally finite mass; im_local (2), (1) give ∂A − B IM.

subproblem.title: Cycles of finite mass with the integer slice property are integer multiplicity (White’s tangent-plane argument)
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT) and (VO). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; they are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. Let d ∈ ℕ and assume CL(d) (CL(d) denotes: for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), T is integer multiplicity; BR(d) denotes: for all P, open U and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every such W, ∂R is integer multiplicity.) A current Y ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) has the integer slice property (ISP) if for all admissible representations (μ, ξ) of Y and (μ', ξ') of ∂Y in ℝ^P (Borel measures finite on compact sets; a.e. strongly measurable fields of (d+1)- resp. d-vectors with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; Y(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ and ∂Y(η) = ∫ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms) and every Lipschitz f : ℝ^P → ℝ, for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, every pair of currents A ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P), B ∈ 𝒟_d(ℝ^P) with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ and B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ' for all test forms has ∂A − B integer multiplicity. If Γ ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) has ∂Γ = 0, M(Γ) < ∞, compact support and ISP, then Γ is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, V6–V12, V14, V15 (B. White's tangent-plane argument replacing Simon's Rectifiability Theorem 6.8.1, with integrality read off from slices), together with the parts of T5 (dilations) and V4(iii) (dilation invariance of the slice property) that this argument uses. The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem, dtc_vanish_off_support; CL(d) is the closure statement in degree d. Siblings used: cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq (restrict_unique), cbr_measure_convergence_tools ((T1), (T2), (MM)), cbr_slice_property_of_weak_limit (slice_limit), cbr_lower_density_of_slice_property (lower_density), cbr_rectifiable_of_approx_tangent (rectifiable). n := d + 1 ≥ 1, Hⁿ := μHE[n], ω_n := unitBallVolume n, ‖ω‖_∞ := sup|ω(x)|; for n-vectors |ζ| is the dual norm. ISP is the integer slice property of the statement. For a current X in ℝ^P with an admissible representation (μ, ξ) and a Borel set E, X⌞E(ω) := ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ defines a current (linear; |X⌞E(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞μ(tsupport ω) gives sequential continuity) with M_W(X⌞E) ≤ μ(W ∩ E); by restrict_unique it does not depend on the admissible representation. If n > P all n-currents vanish and Γ = 0 is IM (empty IMRep); the argument below also covers this case (then μ_Γ = 0 in step 3).

Step 1 (dilations, parent T5). For a ∈ ℝ^P and λ > 0 let η(y) := λ⁻¹(y − a) (an affine bijection, proper, inverse y ↦ a + λy) and, for X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P), η_#X := the affine push-forward of X (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward with linear part λ⁻¹·id and translation −λ⁻¹a): η_#X(ω) = X(η^#ω), (η^#ω)(x) = λ^{−n}ω(η(x)) as n-covectors. (a) ∂η_#X = η_#∂X (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_affinePushforward). (b) η^# maps the admissible forms for M_{η(W)} bijectively onto λ^{−n}·(admissible forms for M_W), so M_{η(W)}(η_#X) = λ^{−n}M_W(X). (c) If (μ, ξ) is an admissible representation of X, the change of variables x = η⁻¹(y) gives η_#X(ω) = ∫ ⟨λ^{−n}ω(η(x)), ξ(x)⟩ dμ(x) = ∫ ξ(η⁻¹y)(ω(y)) d(λ^{−n}η_*μ)(y); so (λ^{−n}η_*μ, ξ∘η⁻¹) is an admissible representation of η_#X, and it is the mass representation if μ(W) = M_W(X) for all open W (by (b)); for Lipschitz f and t ∈ ℝ, the change of variables also gives (η_#X)⌞{f < t} = η_#(X⌞{f∘η < t}) for these representations. (d) Hⁿ(η(A)) = λ^{−n}Hⁿ(A) (translation invariance and scaling of Hausdorff measure). If X = τ(M, θ, ξ) is IM, then η_#X is represented by (η(M), θ∘η⁻¹, ξ∘η⁻¹): by (d), ∫_M θ(x)⟨λ^{−n}ω(η x), ξ(x)⟩ dHⁿ(x) = ∫_{η(M)} θ(η⁻¹y)⟨ω(y), ξ(η⁻¹y)⟩ dHⁿ(y); η(M) is Borel and countably n-rectifiable (compose Lipschitz parametrizations with η; η maps Hⁿ-null sets to Hⁿ-null sets); θ∘η⁻¹ is Borel, positive and locally integrable on η(M); ξ∘η⁻¹ is a.e. strongly measurable; and since blowUpMap (η x) r (η y) = (λr)⁻¹(y − x) = blowUpMap x (λr) y, the approximate tangent space of η(M) at η(x) equals that of M at x. So η_# preserves integer multiplicity.

Step 2 (dilation invariance of ISP, parent V4(iii)). Let X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂X = 0, locally finite mass and ISP, (μ_X, ξ_X) its (REP) representation, and η as in step 1; then X' := η_#X has ISP. Proof: ∂X' = 0 by step 1(a). Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X', ∂X' and f L-Lipschitz; f∘η is (L/λ)-Lipschitz. ISP of X instantiated with (μ_X, ξ_X), (0, 0) (admissible for ∂X = 0) and f∘η gives a null set N such that ∂(X⌞{f∘η < t}) − 0 is IM for t ∉ N (X⌞{f∘η < t} is a current, see the preamble). For t ∉ N and A, B with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(ω) dμ, B(η') = ∫_{f<t} ξ'(η') dμ': restrict_unique (U := ℝ^P) with the two admissible representations (μ, ξ) and (λ^{−n}η_*μ_X, ξ_X∘η⁻¹) of X' (and (0, 0)) gives A = (η_#X)⌞{f < t} = η_#(X⌞{f∘η < t}) (step 1(c)); restrict_unique with (μ', ξ') and (0, 0), both representing ∂X' = 0, gives B = 0. Hence ∂A − B = ∂η_#(X⌞{f∘η<t}) = η_#∂(X⌞{f∘η<t}) is IM by step 1(a), (d).

Step 3 (V6, representation of Γ). Γ has finite mass, so (REP) gives (μ_Γ, ξ_Γ): μ_Γ(W) = M_W(Γ) for open W, μ_Γ(ℝ^P) = M(Γ) < ∞, |ξ_Γ| ≤ 1, Γ(ω) = ∫ ξ_Γ(ω) dμ_Γ. Replacing ξ_Γ by a strongly measurable (Borel) function equal to it μ_Γ-a.e. and then by ζ ↦ ζ/max(1, |ζ|) of it (which changes it only on a μ_Γ-null set) we may assume ξ_Γ is Borel with |ξ_Γ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| everywhere; the representation and the mass identities are unaffected; since ∂Γ = 0, boundaryMassOn(Γ, W) = M_W(0) = 0, so the last clause of (REP) gives μ_Γ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0. Let η₀ > 0 be the constant of lower_density for (P, d). lower_density (C := Γ, μ := μ_Γ, ξ := ξ_Γ; ∂Γ = 0, ISP Γ) gives Θ(x) := liminf_{r↓0} μ_Γ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ η₀ for μ_Γ-a.e. x; Θ is Borel: for fixed r > 0, x ↦ μ_Γ(B_r(x)) is lower semicontinuous (if x_m → x then 1_{B_r(x)} ≤ liminf_m 1_{B_r(x_m)} pointwise; Fatou), and r ↦ μ_Γ(B_r(x)) is left continuous (B_r(x) = ⋃_{s<r}B_s(x)), so Θ(x) = lim_m inf_{r ∈ ℚ∩(0,1/m)} μ_Γ(B_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) is a countable lim/inf of Borel functions. Let M₀ := {x ∈ spt Γ : Θ(x) ≥ η₀} (Borel). μ_Γ(ℝ^P ∖ spt Γ) = 0 (for open G disjoint from spt Γ, μ_Γ(G) = M_G(Γ) = 0 by (VO)), so μ_Γ(ℝ^P ∖ M₀) = 0. For x ∈ M₀ the upper density with closed balls satisfies limsup_r μ_Γ(B̄_r(x))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≥ Θ(x) ≥ η₀, so SimonGMT Chapter01 simon_theorem_3_3 (density comparison; Simon's Hⁿ equals μHE[n] by SimonGMT simonHausdorffMeasureReal_nat_eq_euclideanHausdorffMeasure) gives η₀Hⁿ(M₀) ≤ μ_Γ(ℝ^P) < ∞. Thus μ_Γ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M₀ (if Hⁿ(E ∩ M₀) = 0 then μ_Γ(E) ≤ μ_Γ(E ∩ M₀) + μ_Γ(ℝ^P ∖ M₀) = 0), and by Radon–Nikodym (Hⁿ⌞M₀ finite) μ_Γ = θHⁿ⌞M₀ with θ ≥ 0 Borel and ∫θ dHⁿ⌞M₀ = M(Γ). Put M' := M₀ ∩ {θ > 0} (Borel; μ_Γ(M₀ ∖ M') = 0) and τ := θξ_Γ (a.e. strongly measurable for Hⁿ⌞M'). Then Γ(ω) = ∫_{M'}⟨ω, τ⟩ dHⁿ. Moreover |ξ_Γ| = 1 μ_Γ-a.e.: for open G, μ_Γ(G) = M_G(Γ) = sup_ω ∫ ξ_Γ(ω) dμ_Γ ≤ ∫_G |ξ_Γ| dμ_Γ ≤ μ_Γ(G), so ∫_G (1 − |ξ_Γ|) dμ_Γ = 0 for every open G, hence (outer regularity of the finite measure (1 − |ξ_Γ|)μ_Γ) 1 − |ξ_Γ| = 0 μ_Γ-a.e. Hence |τ| = θ Hⁿ-a.e. on M'. If μ_Γ = 0 then Γ = 0 is IM and we are done; assume Hⁿ(M') > 0 in what follows (the steps below are pointwise statements at Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M').

Step 4 (V7, good points). For Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M': (i) limsup_{r↓0} Hⁿ(M' ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 1 (SimonGMT simon_theorem_3_26_i, Hⁿ(M') < ∞); (ii) a is a Lebesgue point of τ for Hⁿ⌞M' with closed balls: Hⁿ(M' ∩ B̄_r(a))⁻¹∫_{M'∩B̄_r(a)}|τ − τ(a)| dHⁿ → 0 (Mathlib VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub for the Besicovitch Vitali family of the finite measure Hⁿ⌞M', and Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt to pass to radii r ↓ 0); (iii) Θ(a) ≥ η₀ and 0 < θ(a) = |τ(a)| < ∞. Fix such a; τ₀ := τ(a), θ₀ := θ(a). Since |θ − θ₀| ≤ |τ − τ₀| a.e. on M', μ_Γ(B_r(a)) ≤ θ₀Hⁿ(M' ∩ B_r(a)) + ∫_{M'∩B̄_r(a)}|τ − τ₀| dHⁿ = θ₀Hⁿ(M' ∩ B_r(a)) + o(rⁿ) (by (i), (ii)); with μ_Γ(B_r(a)) ≥ (η₀/2)ω_nrⁿ for small r (iii) we get Hⁿ(M' ∩ B_r(a)) ≥ (η₀/(4θ₀))ω_nrⁿ for all small r.

Step 5 (V8, blow-ups). Let λ_i > 0, λ_i → 0, η_i := η_{a,λ_i}, Γ_i := η_{i#}Γ and μ_i := Hⁿ⌞η_i(M'). By step 1(c),(d), Γ_i(ω) = ∫_{η_i(M')}⟨ω(y), τ(a + λ_iy)⟩ dHⁿ(y) and μ_i(B_R(0)) = λ_i^{−n}Hⁿ(M' ∩ B_{λ_iR}(a)); so for each R > 0 and all large i, (η₀/(4θ₀))ω_nRⁿ ≤ μ_i(B_R(0)) ≤ 2ω_nRⁿ (step 4), and sup_i μ_i(K) < ∞ for compact K. For ω with tsupport ω ⊆ B_R(0): |Γ_i(ω) − ∫⟨ω, τ₀⟩ dμ_i| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞λ_i^{−n}∫_{M'∩B̄_{λ_iR}(a)}|τ − τ₀| dHⁿ → 0 (step 4 (i), (ii)). By (T1) (U := ℝ^P) a subsequence (not relabeled) has μ_i → ν: ∫ g dμ_i → ∫ g dν for g ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), limsup μ_i(K) ≤ ν(K) for compact K, ν(G) ≤ liminf μ_i(G) for open G. Then Γ_i ⇀ C, where C(ω) := ∫⟨ω, τ₀⟩ dν (a current: |C(ω)| ≤ θ₀‖ω‖_∞ν(tsupport ω)). Properties: (α) ν(B_R(0)) ≤ liminf μ_i(B_R(0)) ≤ ω_nRⁿ for every R > 0 (step 4(i)). (β) ν(B̄_R(0)) ≥ limsup μ_i(B̄_R(0)) ≥ (η₀/(4θ₀))ω_nRⁿ > 0 for all R > 0, so 0 ∈ spt ν. (γ) ∂C = 0: ∂C(φ) = lim ∂Γ_i(φ) = 0 since ∂Γ_i = η_{i#}∂Γ = 0. (δ) For a locally finite measure ν' and a constant n-vector ζ₀, the current Ξ(ω) := ∫⟨ω, ζ₀⟩ dν' has M_G(Ξ) = |ζ₀|ν'(G) for open G (≤ since |⟨ω, ζ₀⟩| ≤ |ω||ζ₀|; ≥ by testing with φβ₀, β₀ a covector with |β₀| = 1 and ⟨β₀, ζ₀⟩ = |ζ₀|, φ ∈ C_c^∞(G; [0, 1]) increasing to 1_G). Hence M_G(C) = θ₀ν(G): (θ₀ν, τ₀/θ₀) is the mass representation of C (admissible, |τ₀/θ₀| = 1).
