subproblem.title: Closure theorem for compactly supported sequences in ℝ^P (CL*): reduction to cycles
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT) and (VO). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; they are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. Let d ∈ ℕ and assume CL(d) and BR(d) (CL(d) denotes: for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), T is integer multiplicity; BR(d) denotes: for all P, open U and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every such W, ∂R is integer multiplicity.) If K ⊆ ℝ^P is compact, T_j ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(ℝ^P) are integer multiplicity with integer multiplicity boundaries ∂T_j, spt T_j ⊆ K for all j, sup_j (M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞ and T_j ⇀ T in ℝ^P, then T is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, the claim (CL*) with V3 (reduction to cycles, including the n = 1 segment construction), V4(o) and V4(i), the "Application" paragraph of V4, and the last sentence of V15. The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem, dtc_vanish_off_support; CL(d), BR(d) are the closure and boundary-rectifiability statements in degree d. Siblings used: cbr_setIntegral_eq_of_integral_eq (restrict_unique), cbr_measure_convergence_tools ((MM)), cbr_isoperimetric_filling (isoperimetric), cbr_slice_property_of_weak_limit (slice_limit), cbr_cycle_isIntegerMultiplicity (cycle_im). n := d + 1, M := mass in ℝ^P, ‖ω‖_∞ := sup|ω(x)|, ISP the integer slice property of the statements of slice_limit and cycle_im.

0. Preliminaries. (i) For an admissible representation (μ, ξ) of a current X in ℝ^P and a Borel set E, X⌞E(ω) := ∫_E ξ(ω) dμ is a current (linear; |X⌞E(ω)| ≤ ‖ω‖_∞μ(tsupport ω), so test-form-convergent sequences are mapped to convergent sequences) with M_W(X⌞E) ≤ μ(W ∩ E). (ii) The zero current is IM (empty IMRep), and by (IMC)(c) differences of IM currents are IM; hence A + B := A − (0 − B) and all integer combinations of IM currents are IM. (iii) |X(ω)| ≤ M(X)‖ω‖_∞; masses are subadditive.
1. Basic properties of T. If tsupport ω ∩ K = ∅ then T_j(ω) = 0 by (VO) (spt T_j ⊆ K), so T(ω) = 0: spt T ⊆ K. By lower semicontinuity (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf, WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), M(T) ≤ liminf M(T_j) < ∞ and M(∂T) ≤ liminf M(∂T_j) < ∞, and ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T; likewise spt ∂T ⊆ K.
2. ∂T is IM. Apply CL(d) in U := ℝ^P to the IM currents ∂T_j ⇀ ∂T: for every open W, M_W(∂T_j) ≤ sup_j M(∂T_j) < ∞ and boundaryMassOn(∂T_j, W) = 0 (by definition if d = 0; if d ≥ 1 it is M_W(∂∂T_j) = M_W(0) = 0).
3. A compactly supported IM filling Y of ∂T (V3). Case n ≥ 2 (d ≥ 1): Z := ∂T is IM with compact support (spt ∂T ⊆ K closed), ∂Z = ∂∂T = 0 and M(Z) < ∞; isoperimetric with m := d − 1 gives an IM Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) with ∂Y = ∂T, M(Y) < ∞ and spt Y inside a bounded thickening of spt ∂T, so spt Y (closed) is compact. Case n = 1 (d = 0): ∂T is an IM 0-current with compact support. Let (M₀, θ, ξ) be an IMRep; H⁰ is the counting measure, so θ ≥ 1 on M₀ and, by (MR), M_G(∂T) = Σ_{x∈M₀∩G}θ(x) for open G; by (VO) this vanishes for open G disjoint from spt ∂T, so M₀ ⊆ spt ∂T ⊆ K, and M₀ is finite (local integrability on the compact set spt ∂T). As in degree 0 the orientation is ±⟨·⟩ (⟨α⟩ := α(∅)) at every point, so ∂T(g) = Σ_{i=1}^N m_i⟨g(x_i)⟩ with x_i ∈ K and m_i ∈ ℤ ∖ {0}. Choose ζ ∈ C_c^∞(ℝ^P) with ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K; then ∂T(ζ) = T(dζ) = lim_j T_j(dζ) = 0 by (VO) (dζ = 0 near K ⊇ spt T_j), so Σ_im_i = 0. Fix x₀ ∉ {x_1, …, x_N}. Segment currents: for x ≠ x₀ let τ := (x − x₀)/|x − x₀|, I := {x₀ + s(x − x₀) : 0 < s < 1} (open segment) and [[x₀, x]](ω) := ∫_I ω(τ) dH¹. It is IM: carrier I (Borel; countably 1-rectifiable as a subset of the range of the Lipschitz map ℝ → ℝ^P, u ↦ x₀ + uτ), mult := 1 on I, orient := (β ↦ β(τ)) (a unit orientation of the line ℝτ: (τ) is orthonormal and spans it); at every y ∈ I, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 1 I y (ℝτ), because blowUpMap y r maps I onto the segment {uτ : −|y − x₀|/r < u < |x − y|/r}, which contains (ℝτ) ∩ tsupport f for small r (f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P)), so ∫_{blowUpMap y r '' I} f dH¹ = ∫_{ℝτ} f dH¹ for small r; H¹(I) = |x − x₀| < ∞. H¹⌞I is the push-forward of Lebesgue measure on (0, |x − x₀|) under the isometric parametrization u ↦ x₀ + uτ, hence ∂[[x₀, x]](g) = ∫_0^{|x−x₀|} dg(x₀ + uτ)(τ) du = ∫_0^{|x−x₀|} (d/du)⟨g(x₀ + uτ)⟩ du = ⟨g(x)⟩ − ⟨g(x₀)⟩. Let Y := Σ_i m_i[[x₀, x_i]], IM by 0(ii); ∂Y(g) = Σ_im_i(⟨g(x_i)⟩ − ⟨g(x₀)⟩) = Σ_im_i⟨g(x_i)⟩ = ∂T(g); spt Y is contained in the convex hull of {x₀, x_1, …, x_N} (compact); M(Y) ≤ Σ_i|m_i||x_i − x₀| < ∞.
4. The cycle Γ := T − Y ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P): ∂Γ = ∂T − ∂Y = 0; spt Γ ⊆ spt T ∪ spt Y is a closed subset of a compact set, hence compact; M(Γ) ≤ M(T) + M(Y) < ∞.
5. ISP of IM currents (V4(i)). Claim: if X ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) and ∂X are IM and both have locally finite mass, then X has ISP. Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of X, ∂X and f L-Lipschitz. (SL) with these data gives currents A_t, B_t with A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B_t(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ', and Z_t := ∂A_t − B_t with M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for open W. For k, m ∈ ℕ, (MM) (constant sequence, G := B_k(0), (a, b) := (−m, m), μ(B_k(0)) < ∞) gives M_{B_k(0)}(Z_t) < ∞ for a.e. t ∈ (−m, m); so for a.e. t, Z_t has locally finite mass. Fix such t. Let R_X = (M_X, θ_X, ζ_X) be an IMRep of X; (IMC)(b) with E := {f < t} gives an IM current A' represented by (M_X ∩ {f < t}, θ_X, ζ_X); restrict_unique (U := ℝ^P; the admissible representations (μ, ξ) and (R_X.measure, ζ_X) of X — admissible by (IMC)(d) — and (0, 0)) gives A_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ζ_X(ω) dR_X.measure = A'(ω), so A_t is IM. In the same way B_t is IM (IMRep of ∂X). ∂A_t = B_t + Z_t has locally finite mass (M_W(B_t) ≤ μ'(W)), so ∂A_t is IM by BR(d) in U := ℝ^P. By (IMC)(c), Z_t = ∂A_t − B_t is IM. Any A, B satisfying the defining formulas equal A_t, B_t (currents are determined by their values), so ∂A − B is IM for a.e. t: X has ISP.
6. Application. Each T_j has ISP by step 5 (T_j and ∂T_j IM with finite mass); Y has ISP by step 5 (Y IM, ∂Y = ∂T IM, finite masses). slice_limit (CL(d), (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL); sup_j(M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) ≤ sup_j(M(T_j) + M(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every W; T_j ⇀ T) shows that T has ISP.
7. Γ has ISP (V4(o)). Let (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') be admissible representations of Γ, ∂Γ and f L-Lipschitz. Let (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}), (μ_Y, ξ_Y), (μ_{∂Y}, ξ_{∂Y}) be (REP) representations (finite masses). ISP of T and of Y, instantiated with these, gives a null set N such that for t ∉ N the slices Z^T_t := ∂(T⌞{f<t}) − (∂T)⌞{f<t} and Z^Y_t := ∂(Y⌞{f<t}) − (∂Y)⌞{f<t} (restriction currents of 0(i) w.r.t. these representations) are IM. Let t ∉ N and A, B with A(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(ω)dμ, B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ'(η)dμ'. Since T = Γ + Y on every test form, restrict_unique with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ, ξ), (μ_Y, ξ_Y) and E := {f < t} gives T⌞{f<t} = A + Y⌞{f<t}; likewise ∂T = ∂Γ + ∂Y gives (∂T)⌞{f<t} = B + (∂Y)⌞{f<t}. Hence ∂A − B = Z^T_t − Z^Y_t, which is IM by (IMC)(c). So Γ has ISP.
8. Conclusion. By cycle_im (CL(d), (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO); ∂Γ = 0, M(Γ) < ∞, spt Γ compact, ISP), Γ is IM. Since T = Γ − (0 − Y) as currents, T is IM by (IMC)(c) (0 is IM). ∎
proof_key_steps: spt T ⊆ K, finite masses; ∂T is IM by CL(d).
Fill ∂T by a compactly supported IM Y: isoperimetric if d ≥ 1, signed segments from a point if d = 0 (total multiplicity 0 by (VO)).
Γ := T − Y is a compactly supported cycle of finite mass.
IM currents with IM boundaries have ISP ((SL), (MM), (IMC)(b),(c), restrict_unique, BR(d)); hence T_j, Y have ISP and T has ISP by slice_limit.
Linearity of restrictions (restrict_unique) gives ISP for Γ.
cycle_im makes Γ IM; T = Γ − (0 − Y) is IM by (IMC)(c).

audit.reason: The proof derives an IM boundary using CL(d), constructs a finite-mass compact filling, and transfers ISP to the resulting cycle through restriction linearity and slice_limit. cycle_im then proves the compact closure conclusion. BR(d) is an explicit hypothesis, so its use introduces no cycle.

subproblem.title: Closure theorem in degree d + 1 from CL(d) and BR(d) by localization (Simon 8.3(1))
subproblem.statement: Assume (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT) and (VO). Here (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) denote the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem and dtc_vanish_off_support; they are not available in this child's environment, so the needed ones appear verbatim as hypotheses of the Lean statement and are discharged by the parent proof. In words: (REP) a current with locally finite mass in an open U has a mass representation (μ, ξ) (μ(W) = M_W for open W, μ(ℝ^P∖U) = 0, μ finite on compacts of U, |ξ| ≤ 1, X(ω) = ∫ξ(ω)dμ, and μ(E) = 0 whenever Hⁿ(E) = 0 if also the boundary has locally finite mass); (MR) M_W(X) = R.measure(W) for an IMRep R of X and open W; (IMC) (a) locality of approximate tangent spaces for nested Borel sets, (b) the restriction of an IMRep to a Borel set is an IMRep of some current, (c) differences of IM currents are IM, (d) IMRep orientations satisfy |orient(x)(α)| ≤ |α| a.e.; (SL) slicing by an L-Lipschitz f of a current represented together with its boundary, with Z_t := ∂(X⌞{f<t}) − (∂X)⌞{f<t} vanishing on forms supported off {f = t}, M_W(Z_t) ≤ L liminf_h h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}) and the integrated bound; (DT) the deformation theorem with its mass and support bounds; (VO) a current vanishes on test forms whose support misses its support. CL(d) denotes: for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_d(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U, and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_d(U), T is integer multiplicity; BR(d) denotes: for all P, open U and integer multiplicity R ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with M_W(∂R) < ∞ for every such W, ∂R is integer multiplicity. Then for every d ∈ ℕ, CL(d) and BR(d) imply CL(d+1): for all P, open U ⊆ ℝ^P and integer multiplicity T_j ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U) with sup_j (M_W(T_j) + boundaryMassOn(T_j, W)) < ∞ for every open W with compact closure in U and T_j ⇀ T ∈ 𝒟_{d+1}(U), T is integer multiplicity.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, Part V, V1 (boundaries) and V2 (localization, Simon Ch. 6, Remark 8.3(1)), reducing CL(d+1) to the compact case (CL*) proved by the sibling cbr_closure_compact_support. The hypotheses (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO) are the exact frozen statements of the parent node's dependency theorems (not available to this child, hence assumed) cmc_exists_massRepresentation, cmc_massOn_eq_imRep_measure, cmc_imRep_locality_restrict_sub, cmc_slice_mass_bounds, cmc_deformation_theorem, dtc_vanish_off_support. Siblings used: cbr_measure_convergence_tools ((T1), (T2), (MM)), cbr_isIntegerMultiplicity_of_local (im_local), cbr_closure_compact_support (closure_compact). n := d + 1 ≥ 1; for currents of degree n, boundaryMassOn(X, W) = M_W(∂X).

Let P ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T_j, T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) with T_j IM, Λ_W := sup_j(M_W(T_j) + M_W(∂T_j)) < ∞ for every open W ⊂⊂ U, and T_j ⇀ T.
1. (V1) For each j, ∂T_j is IM by BR(d) (M_W(∂T_j) ≤ Λ_W < ∞). By lower semicontinuity (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf and WeaklyConvergesOn.boundary), M_W(T) ≤ Λ_W and M_W(∂T) ≤ Λ_W for open W ⊂⊂ U; so T and ∂T have locally finite mass and (REP) gives admissible representations (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T}).
2. Fix x₀ ∈ U and r₀ > 0 with B̄_{2r₀}(x₀) ⊆ U; G := B_{r₀}(x₀) (open, G ⊂⊂ U). Let R_j = (M_j, θ_j, ξ_j) and R'_j be IMReps of T_j and ∂T_j, μ_j := R_j.measure, μ'_j := R'_j.measure. By (MR), μ_j(W) = M_W(T_j) and μ'_j(W) = M_W(∂T_j) for open W, so sup_j(μ_j(K) + μ'_j(K)) < ∞ for compact K ⊆ U (K lies in some open W ⊂⊂ U); by (IMC)(d) the pairs (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ'_j, R'_j.orient) are admissible representations of T_j, ∂T_j.
3. (T1) applied to (μ_j) in U gives a subsequence (not relabeled; still T_j ⇀ T, still the bounds Λ_W) and a Borel measure μ with μ(ℝ^P ∖ U) = 0, μ(K) < ∞ and limsup_j μ_j(K) ≤ μ(K) for compact K ⊆ U.
4. Slices. f := |· − x₀| (1-Lipschitz). For each j, (SL) for T_j with (μ_j, ξ_j), (μ'_j, R'_j.orient), f, L := 1 gives A_{j,t}(ω) = ∫_{f<t}ξ_j(ω)dμ_j, B_{j,t}, and Z_{j,t} := ∂A_{j,t} − B_{j,t} with Z_{j,t}(η) = 0 when tsupport η ∩ {f = t} = ∅ and M_G(Z_{j,t}) ≤ liminf_h h⁻¹μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}). (MM) with μs j := μ_j, G, (a, b) := (0, r₀), L := 1, Z_j(t) := M_G(Z_{j,t}) (μ_j(G ∩ {0 < f < r₀}) ≤ M_G(T_j) ≤ Λ_G) gives a measurable majorant with finite integral, so liminf_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞ for a.e. r ∈ (0, r₀). Also μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0 for all but countably many r (μ is σ-finite). Fix r ∈ (0, r₀) with both properties and pass to a further subsequence with sup_j M_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞.
5. Total slice mass. Let ω ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(U) with |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. Choose χ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in G and χ = 1 on a neighbourhood of the sphere {f = r} (compact, ⊆ G as r < r₀). Then tsupport((1 − χ)ω) ∩ {f = r} = ∅, so Z_{j,r}((1 − χ)ω) = 0 and Z_{j,r}(ω) = Z_{j,r}(χω) ≤ M_G(Z_{j,r}) (χω is admissible for M_G). Hence M(Z_{j,r}) := M_U(Z_{j,r}) ≤ M_G(Z_{j,r}).
6. T'_j := A_{j,r} = T_j⌞B_r(x₀) is IM: (IMC)(b) with E := B_r(x₀) gives an IMRep (M_j ∩ B_r(x₀), θ_j, ξ_j) of a current whose values are ∫_{M_j∩B_r(x₀)}θ_jξ_j(ω)dH^n = A_{j,r}(ω). If tsupport ω ∩ B̄_r(x₀) = ∅ then T'_j(ω) = 0, so spt T'_j ⊆ K := B̄_r(x₀). M(T'_j) ≤ μ_j(B_r(x₀)) ≤ Λ_G, and ∂T'_j = B_{j,r} + Z_{j,r} with M(B_{j,r}) ≤ μ'_j(B_r(x₀)) ≤ Λ_G; so sup_j(M(T'_j) + M(∂T'_j)) ≤ 2Λ_G + sup_jM_G(Z_{j,r}) < ∞.
7. Convergence. Let A_r := T⌞B_r(x₀) be the current ω ↦ ∫_{f<r}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T (e.g. the first family of (SL) for T with (μ_T, ξ_T), (μ_{∂T}, ξ_{∂T})). (T2) (Xs := T_j with (μ_j, ξ_j); X := T with (μ_T, ξ_T); the limit μ of step 3, μ{f = r} = μ(∂B_r(x₀)) = 0; f continuous) gives T'_j(ω) → A_r(ω) for all ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
8. Extension to ℝ^P. Fix ζ ∈ C^∞(ℝ^P; [0, 1]) with compact support in U and ζ = 1 on a neighbourhood of K. Define T̂'_j(ω) := T'_j(ζω) and Â_r(ω) := A_r(ζω) for ω ∈ 𝒟^n(ℝ^P); these are currents in ℝ^P (multiplication by ζ preserves test-form convergence and maps into 𝒟^n(U)). T̂'_j is IM: the IMRep (M_j ∩ B_r(x₀), θ_j, ξ_j), viewed in ℝ^P (Borel carrier, ∫_{M_j∩B_r∩K'}θ_j ≤ μ_j(K) < ∞ for every compact K'), represents it because ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀). spt T̂'_j ⊆ K, M(T̂'_j) ≤ M(T'_j) (ζω admissible when ω is). For η ∈ 𝒟^{n−1}(ℝ^P), ∂T̂'_j(η) = T'_j(ζdη) = T'_j(d(ζη)) − T'_j(dζ ∧ η) = ∂T'_j(ζη) by (VO) (dζ = 0 near K ⊇ spt T'_j), so M(∂T̂'_j) ≤ M(∂T'_j). Hence sup_j(M(T̂'_j) + M(∂T̂'_j)) < ∞, and T̂'_j(ω) = T'_j(ζω) → A_r(ζω) = Â_r(ω): T̂'_j ⇀ Â_r in ℝ^P.
9. ∂T̂'_j is IM by BR(d) in U := ℝ^P (T̂'_j IM; M_W(∂T̂'_j) ≤ M(∂T'_j) < ∞ for every W).
10. By closure_compact (CL(d), BR(d), (REP), (MR), (IMC), (SL), (DT), (VO); the compact set K, IM currents T̂'_j with IM boundaries, spt T̂'_j ⊆ K, bounded total masses, T̂'_j ⇀ Â_r), Â_r is IM.
11. For ω ∈ 𝒟^n(B_r(x₀)): Â_r(ω) = A_r(ζω) = A_r(ω) = ∫_{B_r(x₀)}ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = ∫ξ_T(ω)dμ_T = T(ω) (ζ = 1 on B_r(x₀), and ω vanishes off B_r(x₀)). So T|_{B_r(x₀)} = Â_r|_{B_r(x₀)}, which is IM by part (2) of im_local (in ℝ^P, V := B_r(x₀)). Since x₀ ∈ U was arbitrary (with some r > 0, B_r(x₀) ⊆ U) and T has locally finite mass (step 1), part (1) of im_local shows that T is IM. (If n > P all n-currents vanish and the argument still applies; T = 0 is IM.) ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂T_j IM by BR(d); T, ∂T have locally finite mass (lower semicontinuity).
IMRep measures of T_j converge on U along a subsequence (T1).
Slicing by |· − x₀| and (MM) give a radius r with bounded slice masses and μ(∂B_r) = 0.
T_j⌞B_r(x₀) are IM, supported in B̄_r(x₀), with bounded masses and boundary masses, and converge to T⌞B_r(x₀) (T2).
Extend to ℝ^P by a cutoff; boundaries are IM by BR(d); closure_compact makes the extended limit IM.
It agrees with T on B_r(x₀); im_local (2) then (1) shows T is IM.

audit.reason: The localization proof supplies every hypothesis of closure_compact: IM currents and boundaries, common compact support, uniform total mass bounds, and weak convergence after extension. Domain restriction and locality recover CL(d+1). Together with closure_zero and boundary_im, this proves both exact parent conjuncts by induction.
